   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 October 2003 establishing a scheme for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading within the Community and amending Council Directive 96/61/EC (Text with EEA relevance)», the European Union's emissions trading law (the EU ETS). It is read here in its consolidated form, headed «Consolidated TEXT: 32003L0087 — EN — 01.03.2024», so amendments made after that consolidation are not reflected. Its jurisdictional scope is the Union through its Member States: «This Directive is addressed to the Member States.» Its field is set by its annexes: «This Directive shall apply to the activities listed in Annexes I and III, and to the greenhouse gases listed in Annex II.»

What the Directive says is taken from its own text. What it may mean for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Directive puts a price on greenhouse gas emissions. Its purpose, in the consolidated text: «This Directive also provides for the reductions of greenhouse gas emissions to be increased so as to contribute to the levels of reductions that are considered scientifically necessary to avoid dangerous climate change.» Three parts reach freight. Aviation and maritime transport are covered by their own articles: «Articles 3b to 3g shall apply to the allocation and issue of allowances in respect of the aviation activities listed in Annex I. Articles 3ga to 3gg shall apply in respect of the maritime transport activities listed in Annex I.» The maritime allowance count shrinks over time at a stated rate: «The linear factor shall be 4,3 % from 2024 to 2027 and 4,4 % from 2028.» Aviation fuel is tied to the Union's renewable energy law in the allowance support rules: «95 % of the remaining price differential between the use of fossil kerosene and renewable fuels of non-biological origin compliant with Article 25 of Directive (EU) 2018/2001, used in aviation». A third part, Chapter IVa, is headed «EMISSIONS TRADING SYSTEM FOR BUILDINGS, ROAD TRANSPORT AND ADDITIONAL SECTORS».

Maritime transport is covered in shares of each voyage: «The allocation of allowances and the application of surrender requirements in respect of maritime transport activities shall apply in respect of fifty percent (50 %) of the emissions from ships performing voyages departing from a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State and arriving at a port of call outside the jurisdiction of a Member State, fifty percent (50 %) of the emissions from ships performing voyages departing from a port of call outside the jurisdiction of a Member State and arriving at a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State, one hundred percent (100 %) of emissions from ships performing voyages departing from a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State and arriving at a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State, and one hundred percent (100 %) of emissions from ships within a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State.» The duty falls on the shipping company: «‘shipping company’ means the shipowner or any other organisation or person, such as the manager or the bareboat charterer, that has assumed the responsibility for the operation of the ship from the shipowner and that, on assuming such responsibility, has agreed to take over all the duties and responsibilities imposed by the International Management Code for the Safe Operation of Ships and for Pollution Prevention». The duty phases in: «Shipping companies shall be liable to surrender allowances according to the following schedule: (a) 40 % of verified emissions reported for 2024 that would be subject to surrender requirements in accordance with Article 12; (b) 70 % of verified emissions reported for 2025 that would be subject to surrender requirements in accordance with Article 12; (c) 100 % of verified emissions reported for 2026 and each year thereafter in accordance with Article 12.»

The effective date: «This Directive shall enter into force on the day of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .» The record of the Directive gives the first date of entry into force as «content="2003-10-25"
      datatype="xsd:date"».

*Analytical inference:* an ocean carrier or other shipping company must surrender allowances for the emissions of a covered voyage, and since the 2026 emissions year the whole of the covered emissions counts. A freight business is not the shipping company by default. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any contract of the business makes it the entity that has taken over the purchase of fuel or the operation of a ship.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

COST ALERT: the cost of allowances for covered voyages is in force: shipping companies surrender allowances for 100 % of verified emissions reported for 2026 and each year after. The Directive does not say how that cost reaches a carrier's customer; the one pass-through clause it contains runs from the shipping company to the entity that has taken over fuel purchase or operation of the ship (Section 8). A date inside the next 30 days does not fall on a freight business. The nearest steps run on public bodies: «No later than 31 December 2026, the Commission shall present a report to the European Parliament and to the Council in which it shall examine the feasibility and economic, environmental and social impacts of the inclusion in this Directive of emissions from ships, including offshore ships, below 5 000 gross tonnage but not below 400 gross tonnage».

- A carrier-relations lead asks each ocean carrier in the rate agreements, at the next rate review, whether an allowance cost under the EU ETS is added to the rate and how it is calculated.
- A pricing lead records, on each quote that includes a sea leg to or from a port under the jurisdiction of a Member State, which shipping company performs the voyage and whether the rate includes an allowance charge.
- A contracts lead lists the charters and space contracts in which the business decides the cargo carried, the route or the speed, or buys the fuel, at the next renewal of each such contract, because the Directive gives the shipping company a right of reimbursement in that case.
- A pricing lead for road transport checks whether the Commission's notice under Article 30k was published by 15 July 2026, before the next road rate quote run, to know whether the road fuel allowance system starts surrender on 1 January 2028 or later.

The reasons are quoted in Section 8. *Analytical inference:* the first three steps rest on the shipping company duty and the reimbursement clause; the fourth rests on the Article 30k conditions. The Directive requires none of them of a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any charge in a rate card is a pass-through of allowance costs and whether the contract allows it.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Directive names Member States, administering authorities, shipping companies, aircraft operators, operators of installations, regulated entities and the Commission. A shipping company is defined in Section 2. The authority that supervises it is named by a rule on the company's registration: «in the case of a shipping company registered in a Member State, the Member State in which the shipping company is registered». Aircraft are covered through the operator: «‘aircraft operator’ means the person who operates an aircraft at the time it performs an aviation activity listed in Annex I or, where that person is not known or is not identified by the owner of the aircraft, the owner of the aircraft». The road fuel chapter reaches fuel suppliers, not final consumers: «any natural or legal person, except for any final consumer of the fuels, that engages in the activity referred to in Annex III and that falls within one of the following categories:». A freight forwarder is not named.

The Directive links a shipping company to its customers in one place: «Member States shall take the necessary measures to ensure that when the ultimate responsibility for the purchase of the fuel, or the operation of the ship, or both, is assumed by an entity other than the shipping company pursuant to a contractual arrangement, the shipping company is entitled to reimbursement from that entity for the costs arising from the surrender of allowances.» It defines the operation of a ship: «‘Operation of the ship’ for the purposes of this Article means determining the cargo carried or the route and the speed of the ship.» The company stays liable: «The shipping company shall remain the entity responsible for surrendering allowances as required under Articles 3gb and 12 and for overall compliance with the provisions of national law transposing this Directive.»

*Analytical inference:* a freight business sits outside the compliance chain unless it assumes the purchase of fuel or the operation of a ship by contract, and then the reimbursement right runs from the shipping company to it. The clause states a right of the shipping company, not a surcharge on cargo. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a time charter, a space charter or a slot contract of the business assumes the operation of the ship as the Directive defines it.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no guidance document is held for this Directive.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Directive sets many dated reviews and acts. Acts already due (dates passed): «The Commission shall, by 31 December 2023, by means of implementing acts establish a list of neighbouring container transhipment ports and update that list by 31 December every two years thereafter.» and «before 1 February 2024, a list of shipping companies which performed a maritime transport activity listed in Annex I that fell within the scope set out in Article 3ga on or with effect from 1 January 2024».

Items still ahead:
- Shipping company lists: «before 1 February 2026 and every two years thereafter, an updated list to reattribute shipping companies registered in a Member State to another administering authority in respect of a shipping company» (the 2026 date has passed) and «before 1 February 2028 and every four years thereafter, an updated list to reattribute shipping companies that are not registered in a Member State».
- Smaller ships: «No later than 31 December 2026, the Commission shall present a report to the European Parliament and to the Council in which it shall examine the feasibility and economic, environmental and social impacts of the inclusion in this Directive of emissions from ships, including offshore ships, below 5 000 gross tonnage but not below 400 gross tonnage», built on «building, in particular, on the analysis accompanying the review of Regulation (EU) 2015/757 due by 31 December 2024».
- Maritime allowances: «From 1 January 2026 and 1 January 2027 respectively, the quantity of allowances shall be increased to take into account the coverage of greenhouse gas emissions other than CO 2 emissions from maritime transport activities and the coverage of emissions of offshore ships» (the 1 January 2026 step has started, the 1 January 2027 step is ahead).
- Aviation: «Before 1 January 2027 and every three years thereafter, the Commission shall report to the European Parliament and to the Council on progress in the ICAO negotiations to implement the global market-based measure» and «by 31 January 2028 for emissions in the period 2024 to 2026».
- Road fuel allowances: «By 30 June 2027, the Commission shall publish the Union-wide quantity of allowances for 2028 and, if required, the adjusted linear reduction factor.»
- Postponement test: «By 15 July 2026, the Commission shall publish a notice in the Official Journal of the European Union concerning whether one or both of the following conditions have been met» (date passed). If a condition is met, the Commission's later review moves too: «the deadline for the Commission to report to the European Parliament and to the Council shall be put back to 1 January 2029».
- Maritime review: «No later than 30 September 2028, the Commission shall assess the appropriateness of extending the application of Article 3ga(3), second subparagraph, beyond 31 December 2030 and, if appropriate, submit a legislative proposal to that effect.» And if the International Maritime Organization has not acted by 2028, «the Commission shall submit a report to the European Parliament and to the Council in which it shall examine the need to apply the allocation of allowances and surrender requirements in respect of more than fifty percent (50 %) of the emissions from ships performing voyages between a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State and a port of call outside the jurisdiction of a Member State».
- Road review: «By 1 January 2028, the Commission shall report to the European Parliament and to the Council on the implementation of the provisions of this Chapter with regard to their effectiveness, administration and practical app» and «By 31 October 2031, the Commission shall assess the feasibility of integrating the sectors covered by Annex III to this Directive into the».

*Analytical inference:* the 2028 maritime steps are the point at which the 50 % share on voyages to or from outside ports could be raised, and the 2026 smaller ships report could widen the vessels covered; the text gives no content for either proposal. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the Article 30k notice was published and which conditions it found met, because that decides whether road fuel allowances start in 2027 or 2028.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The first question is which voyages and ships count. The share depends on where a voyage starts and ends, and a stop only counts if it is a port of call: «‘port of call’ means the port where a ship stops to load or unload cargo or to embark or disembark passengers, or the port where an offshore ship stops to relieve the crew; stops for the sole purposes of refuelling, obtaining supplies, relieving the crew of a ship other than an offshore ship, going into dry-dock or making repairs to the ship, its equipment, or both, stops in port because the ship is in need of assistance or in distress, ship-to-ship transfers carried out outside ports, stops for the sole purpose of taking shelter from adverse weather or rendered necessary by search and rescue activities, and stops of containerships in a neighbouring container transhipment port listed in the implementing act adopted pursuant to Article 3ga(2) are excluded». The Commission lists the neighbouring container transhipment ports by a test: «Those implementing acts shall list a port as a neighbouring container transhipment port where the share of transhipment of containers, measured in twenty-foot equivalent units, exceeds 65 % of the total container traffic of that port during the most recent twelve-month period for which relevant data are available and where that port is located outside the Union but less than 300 nautical miles from a port under the jurisdiction of a Member State.» The second question is which Member State administers a shipping company (Section 4). The third is who the regulated entity is under the road fuel chapter.

*Analytical inference:* a stop for fuel, supplies, repairs or shelter is not a port of call, and a containership stop in a listed neighbouring transhipment port is excluded from the definition, so the first and last ports of call decide the 50 % or 100 % share. *Legal Confirmation Required:* how a given route with a transhipment port outside the Union is treated under the Commission's list of neighbouring container transhipment ports.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Surrender and the excess penalty. The annual duty: «The Member States, administering Member States and administering authorities in respect of a shipping company shall ensure that, by 30 September each year: (a) the operator of each installation surrenders a number of allowances that is equal to the total emissions from that installation during the preceding calendar year, as verified in accordance with Article 15; (b) each aircraft operator surrenders a number of allowances that is equal to its total emissions during the preceding calendar year, as verified in accordance with Article 15; (c) each shipping company surrenders a number of allowances that is equal to its total emissions during the preceding calendar year, as verified in accordance with Article 3ge.» The maritime phase-in is in Section 2. Ice-class ships get a reduction: «shipping companies may surrender 5 % fewer allowances than their verified emissions released until 31 December 2030 from ice-class ships». The supervising State of a company not registered in a Member State is set by port calls: «in the case of a shipping company that is not registered in a Member State, the Member State with the greatest estimated number of port calls from voyages performed by that shipping company in the preceding four monitoring years and falling within the scope set out in Article 3ga». Maritime emissions are monitored through another law: «the administering authority in respect of a shipping company shall ensure that a shipping company under its responsibility monitors and reports the relevant parameters during a reporting period, and submits to it aggregated emissions data at company level in accordance with Chapter II of Regulation (EU) 2015/757».

Cost transfer. «Member States shall take the necessary measures to ensure that when the ultimate responsibility for the purchase of the fuel, or the operation of the ship, or both, is assumed by an entity other than the shipping company pursuant to a contractual arrangement, the shipping company is entitled to reimbursement from that entity for the costs arising from the surrender of allowances.»

Road fuel allowances. Permits first: «Member States shall ensure that, from 1 January 2025, no regulated entity carries out the activity referred to in Annex III unless that regulated entity holds a permit issued by a competent authority». Surrender follows: «From 1 January 2028, Member States shall ensure that, by 31 May each year, the regulated entity surrenders an amount of allowances covered by this Chapter that is equal to the regulated entity’s total emissions, corresponding to the quantity of fuels released for consumption pursuant to Annex III, during the preceding calendar year». The Directive watches the cost pass-through: «From 1 January 2028, Member States shall ensure that, by 30 April each year until 2030, each regulated entity reports the average share of costs related to the surrender of allowances under this Chapter which it passed on to consumers for the preceding year.» The postponement rule: «by way of derogation from Article 30d(1) and (2), the start of auctioning of allowances under this Chapter shall be postponed to 2028» and «the deadline for initial surrendering of allowances shall be put back to 31 May 2029 for total emissions in the year 2028».

Allowance validity. «Allowances issued from 1 January 2013 onwards shall be valid indefinitely.» «Allowances issued from 1 January 2021 onwards shall include an indication showing in which ten-year period beginning from 1 January 2021 they were issued, and be valid for emissions from the first year of that period onwards.»

Industrial free allocation. The border carbon factor for goods listed in Regulation (EU) 2023/956 falls over time: «From 2034, no CBAM factor shall apply.» This concerns installations, and the Directive's reduction runs «subject to the application of provisions referred to in Article 36(2), point (b), of that Regulation, shall be equal to 97,5 % in 2026, 95 % in 2027, 90 % in 2028, 77,5 % in 2029, 51,5 % in 2030, 39 % in 2031, 26,5 % in 2032 and 14 % in 2033».

Penalty summary. «The excess emissions penalty shall be EUR 100 for each tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent emitted for which the operator or aircraft operator has not surrendered allowances.» «The penalties set out in paragraph 3 shall also apply in respect of shipping companies.» The penalty grows over time: «The excess emissions penalty relating to allowances issued from 1 January 2013 onwards shall increase in accordance with the European index of consumer prices.» Names are public: «Member States shall ensure the publication of the names of operators, aircraft operators and shipping companies that are in breach of requirements to surrender sufficient allowances under this Directive.» Paying does not end the duty: «Payment of the excess emissions penalty shall not release the operator or aircraft operator from the obligation to surrender an amount of allowances equal to those excess emissions when surrendering allowances in relation to the following calendar year.»

*Analytical inference:* the surrender duty, the penalty and the publication of names fall on shipping companies, aircraft operators, installation operators and regulated entities, not on a forwarder. The only clause that moves allowance cost between parties is the reimbursement right of the shipping company, and the road fuel chapter has a report on the share of cost passed on to consumers. The Directive states no allowance price and no surcharge for cargo, so how the cost reaches a rate is a gap. No phase-in of the penalty is stated in Article 16. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a reimbursement under the cost transfer clause or a charge in a rate card is allowed under the contract and national law, and which Member State supervises the carrier.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Directive sets allowance duties for operators, not rules for products a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Registration and reporting run through the carrier's supervising authority and the registry. Shipping companies report emissions at company level (Section 8) and are listed by the Commission, which assigns each one an administering authority. The road fuel chapter has its own reporting: «Member States shall ensure that each regulated entity holding a permit in accordance with Article 30b on 1 January 2025 reports its historical emissions for the year 2024 by 30 April 2025.» Aviation offset cancellations are dated: «The cancellation shall take place by 31 January 2025 for emissions in the period 2021 to 2023 and by 31 January 2028 for emissions in the period 2024 to 2026.»

*Analytical inference:* the Directive states no registration or report by a freight business. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a business that holds a shipping company or aircraft operator role through its own vessels or aircraft has to register with an administering authority.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

COST ALERT: the Directive builds its systems into carriers and fuel suppliers. For a freight business the working need is evidence of what the carrier charges and why. The Directive's own review of cost effects: «The Commission shall also monitor impacts regarding, inter alia, possible transport cost increases, market distortions and changes in port traffic, such as port evasion and shifts of transhipment hubs».

- A pricing lead keeps, per ocean carrier, a line in the rate sheet that shows whether the rate includes an allowance charge, its basis and the date it was last confirmed, filled on each rate review.
- A contracts lead adds to each charter or space contract a clause, as each contract comes up for renewal, that states who bears the cost of surrendering allowances and who decides the cargo carried, the route and the speed, because the Directive ties the reimbursement right to who assumes those decisions.

*Analytical inference:* both steps follow from the cost transfer clause and from the Commission's duty to watch transport cost increases. The Directive states no format for a surcharge. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a clause allocating allowance cost is consistent with the national law that carries the Directive into force.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

The Directive contains several exceptions. Ice-class ships get a temporary reduction (Section 8). A share of allowances is attributed to some Member States: «Until 31 December 2030, a share of allowances shall be attributed to Member States with a ratio of shipping companies that would have been under their responsibility pursuant to Article 3gf compared to their respective population in 2020 and based on data available for the period from 2018 to 2020, above 15 shipping companies per million inhabitants.» Carbon tax states may exempt road fuel entities for a time: «Until 31 December 2030, by way of derogation from paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article, where a regulated entity established in a given Member State is subject to a national carbon tax in force for the years 2027 to 2030, covering the activity referred to in Annex III, the competent authority of the Member State concerned may exempt that regulated entity from the obligation to surrender allowances».

*Analytical inference:* the carbon tax derogation lets a Member State exempt a regulated entity from surrender but does not stop a national carbon tax from applying. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the Member States where the business buys road fuel have used the derogation.

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

The Directive was made in 2003: the consolidated text carries the later amendments. The effective date is by publication, and the record gives the first entry into force: «content="2003-10-25"
      datatype="xsd:date"».

- 13 October 2003: Directive made, as the title states
- 25 October 2003: Directive enters into force (first entry-into-force field of the record)
- 1 January 2013: excess emissions penalty indexation applies to allowances issued from this date
- 1 January 2021: allowances carry a ten-year period indication
- 31 December 2023: Commission list of neighbouring container transhipment ports due (date passed)
- 1 January 2024: shipping companies' scope begins; 40 % of verified 2024 emissions to be surrendered (date passed)
- 31 December 2024: review of Regulation (EU) 2015/757 due (date passed)
- 1 January 2025: road fuel permits required (date passed); 70 % of verified 2025 emissions is the surrender share for that year
- 31 January 2025: aviation offset cancellation for the 2021 to 2023 emissions (date passed)
- 30 April 2025: road fuel entities report 2024 emissions (date passed)
- 1 January 2026: coverage of greenhouse gases other than carbon dioxide for maritime transport; 100 % of verified emissions to be surrendered (in force)
- 15 July 2026: Commission notice on whether road fuel allowances are postponed to 2028 (date passed)
- 31 December 2026: Commission report on smaller ships
- 1 January 2027: offshore ships coverage; Commission report on ICAO progress due before this date
- 30 June 2027: Commission publishes the 2028 quantity of allowances for road fuel
- 1 January 2028: road fuel surrender duty and the Commission review of that chapter; maritime allowance linear factor rises
- 31 January 2028: aviation offset cancellation for the 2024 to 2026 emissions
- 30 September 2028: Commission assessment of extending the share for Member States beyond 2030
- 1 January 2029: Commission report date if the postponement applies
- 31 December 2030: ice-class reduction, the Member State share and road fuel carbon tax derogation end
- 31 October 2031: Commission assessment of integrating road fuel into the main scheme
- 2034: no border carbon factor applies (from the year 2034)

*Analytical inference:* the primary deadline for shipping companies is the annual surrender by 30 September; the stored phase-in dates of 2024, 2025 and 2026 are passed and the full 100 % share has applied since the 2026 emissions year. The consolidated text read here is dated 01.03.2024, so any later change to these dates needs a check of the current text.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «Directive (EU) 2023/959 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 10 May 2023 amending Directive 2003/87/EC establishing a system for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading within the Union», the Union's reform of its emissions trading system (the EU ETS). It brings maritime transport into the system and sets up a second system for fuels used in buildings and road transport. What the Directive requires is stated from its own words; what it means for the workspace is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

Its reach for shipping: «The allocation of allowances and the application of surrender requirements in respect of maritime transport activities shall apply in respect of fifty percent (50 %) of the emissions from ships performing voyages departing from a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State and arriving at a port of call outside the jurisdiction of a Member State, fifty percent (50 %) of the emissions from ships performing voyages departing from a port of call outside the jurisdiction of a Member State and arriving at a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State, one hundred percent (100 %) of emissions from ships performing voyages departing from a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State and arriving at a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State, and one hundred percent (100 %) of emissions from ships within a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State.»

It enters into force as its final article states: «This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union». The Commission's guidance gives the date: «The new rules entered into force on 5 June 2023.» Member States had to act first: «Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with Article 1 of this Directive by 31 December 2023. They shall apply those measures from 1 January 2024.» For buildings and road transport the date is later: «However, Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with the following articles by 30 June 2024».

*Analytical inference:* the jurisdiction is the Member States' ports and voyages, so the share of a voyage that is priced depends on where it starts and ends; it rests on the 50 and 100 percent sentence quoted above.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Directive makes a shipping company the party responsible: «“shipping company” means the shipowner or any other organisation or person, such as the manager or the bareboat charterer, that has assumed the responsibility for the operation of the ship from the shipowner and that, on assuming such responsibility, has agreed to take over all the duties and responsibilities». Which ships: «In addition to cargo and passengers ship of or above 5 000 GT, offshore and general cargo ship of tonnage of or above 400 GT will be included under MRV scope starting 2025.» «Large offshore ship of tonnage of or above 5 000 GT will be included within ETS scope starting the reporting period 2027.» Which gases: «Only CO 2 emissions will be accounted under ETS scope in the first two years (2024 and 2025), as CH 4 and N 2 O will fall under scope starting 2026.» The industry body ICAP describes the second system: «The EU ETS 2 covers the emissions from the consumption of fuels used for combustion in the road transport and buildings sectors, as well as in small industrial emitters.» «It will cover emissions upstream, meaning the obligation to surrender allowances will fall on the fuel suppliers rather than end-consumers.»

Why it applies to the workspace: ocean carriage on voyages touching the Union carries the shipping company's allowance duty, and road transport fuel is covered by the second system.

*Analytical inference:* ocean legs that start or end in a Union port fall under the 50 or 100 percent shares, and diesel for road transport is covered through the fuel supplier. It rests on the scope and covered-fuel sentences quoted above. The texts held state no surcharge percentage and no price effect on rates.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

COST ALERT: the maritime cost is in force and the Directive says who may pass it on. «when the ultimate responsibility for the purchase of the fuel, or the operation of the ship, or both, is assumed by an entity other than the shipping company pursuant to a contractual arrangement, the shipping company is entitled to reimbursement from that entity for the costs arising from the surrender of allowances.» The Directive defines the term: «‘Operation of the ship’ for the purposes of this Article means determining the cargo carried or the route and the speed of the ship.» The next surrender falls on «shall ensure that, by 30 September each year: (a) the operator of each installation surrenders a number of allowances that is equal to the total emissions from that installation during the preceding calendar year, as verified in accordance with Article 15; (b) each aircraft operator surrenders a number of allowances that is equal to its total emissions during the preceding calendar year, as verified in accordance with Article 15; (c) each shipping company surrenders a number of allowances that is equal to its total emissions during the preceding calendar year, as verified in accordance with Article 3ge.»

- Carrier manager, at the next rate review with each ocean carrier: ask which entity is the shipping company for the ship and whether an allowance cost is shown in the rate, and record whether the carrier relies on the reimbursement sentence above.
- Contracts lead, before signing the next charter or space agreement: mark any arrangement under which the workspace or a client decides the cargo carried, the route or the speed of a ship, because that is the Directive's wording for operation of the ship.
- Pricing lead, before the first quote for 2027 sailings: plan on the basis that the phase-in reaches 100% in 2026 of the verified emissions that would be subject to surrender requirements, as quoted in section 8: «A phased approach for surrendering obligations determination is foreseen, starting at 40% in 2024, 70% in 2025 and reaching 100% by 2026 for the ship types under scope.»
- Fuel buyer, at the next fuel supply renewal: ask each fuel supplier when the second system starts to affect fuel prices, because the Directive text and a later industry report give different start years (section 6).

*Analytical inference:* the reimbursement sentence is the Directive's own route for the cost to move from the shipping company to the entity that decides the fuel purchase or the operation of the ship; the texts held do not say how carriers price it or whether the workspace is such an entity. It rests on the two quoted sentences. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace or a client is an entity that assumes responsibility for the purchase of fuel or the operation of a ship under a contract, and so can be asked to reimburse the shipping company.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The roles. The shipping company is the duty holder (section 2). The authority that administers it: «The administering authority in respect of a shipping company shall be: (a) in the case of a shipping company registered in a Member State, the Member State in which the shipping company is registered; (b) in the case of a shipping company that is not registered in a Member State, the Member State with the greatest estimated number of port calls from voyages performed by that shipping company in the preceding four monitoring years and falling within the scope set out in Article 3ga;» The Commission's guidance says of a bareboat charterer: «The bareboat charterer can be responsible for compliance with ETS and MRV in respect of a given ship only if that bareboat charterer has accepted to assume ISM Code responsibilities in respect of that ship.» ICAP, an industry body, describes the duty holder in the second system as: «Type of entities Entities releasing fuels for consumption (e.g., fuel distributors)».

A forwarder is not named in the text held here; the entities that can reach it are the one that assumes responsibility for the purchase of the fuel or the operation of the ship (section 3) and, for road transport fuel, the fuel supplier's customers.

*Analytical inference:* the workspace is not a duty holder in either system; it can meet the cost through a carrier's rate, through the reimbursement sentence if it assumes responsibility for fuel purchase or ship operation, or through the fuel price. It rests on the role sentences quoted above. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which entity is the shipping company for a given vessel and whether any contract with a carrier makes the workspace an entity that assumes responsibility for the operation of the ship.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

Dated steps and open reviews at the date of this document.

- The start of the second system. The Directive text sets 2027: «From 2027, allowances covered by this Chapter shall be auctioned». An industry body reports a change: «Following a decision by the EU Council and the European Parliament in March 2026, the start date was postponed for one year, to 2028.» The change is not in the Directive text; this document treats 2027 as the Directive's date and 2028 as the industry body's report.
- The check on energy prices: «By 15 July 2026, the Commission shall publish a notice in the Official Journal of the European Union concerning whether one or both of the following conditions have been met». The date has passed; the capture does not say whether the notice was published.
- A report on smaller ships: «No later than 31 December 2026, the Commission shall present a report to the European Parliament and to the Council in which it shall examine the feasibility and economic, environmental and social impacts of the inclusion in this Directive of emissions from ships, including offshore ships, below 5 000 gross tonnage but not below 400 gross tonnage»
- A review of the second system: «By 1 January 2028, the Commission shall report to the European Parliament and to the Council on the implementation of the provisions of this Chapter with regard to their effectiveness, administration and practical application»
- The share for some Member States: «No later than 30 September 2028, the Commission shall assess the appropriateness of extending the application of Article 3ga(3), second subparagraph, beyond 31 December 2030»
- Integration of the two systems: «By 31 October 2031, the Commission shall assess the feasibility of integrating the sectors covered by Annex III to this Directive into the EU ETS covering the sectors listed in Annex I to this Directive.»

*Analytical inference:* the start year of the second system and the report on smaller ships each bear on the dates in this document; the capture states no outcome for either. They rest on the quoted start-year sentences and the smaller ships sentence. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which start year of the second system governs a given fuel supplier, the Directive's text or the later change ICAP reports.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

**Scope and gases.** «Large offshore ship of tonnage of or above 5 000 GT will be included within ETS scope starting the reporting period 2027.»

**Phase-in.** «Shipping companies shall be liable to surrender allowances according to the following schedule: (a) 40 % of verified emissions reported for 2024 that would be subject to surrender requirements in accordance with Article 12; (b) 70 % of verified emissions reported for 2025 that would be subject to surrender requirements in accordance with Article 12; (c) 100 % of verified emissions reported for 2026 and each year thereafter in accordance with Article 12.» «A phased approach for surrendering obligations determination is foreseen, starting at 40% in 2024, 70% in 2025 and reaching 100% by 2026 for the ship types under scope.»

**Surrender.** «shall ensure that, by 30 September each year: (a) the operator of each installation surrenders a number of allowances that is equal to the total emissions from that installation during the preceding calendar year, as verified in accordance with Article 15; (b) each aircraft operator surrenders a number of allowances that is equal to its total emissions during the preceding calendar year, as verified in accordance with Article 15; (c) each shipping company surrenders a number of allowances that is equal to its total emissions during the preceding calendar year, as verified in accordance with Article 3ge.»

**Monitoring and verification.** «the administering authority in respect of a shipping company shall ensure that a shipping company under its responsibility monitors and reports the relevant parameters during a reporting period, and submits to it aggregated emissions data at company level in accordance with Chapter II of Regulation (EU) 2015/757.» «shall ensure that the reporting of aggregated emissions data at shipping company level submitted by a shipping company pursuant to Article 3gd of this Directive is verified in accordance with the verification and accreditation rules set out in Chapter III of Regulation (EU) 2015/757.»

**Cost transfer.** «The shipping company shall remain the entity responsible for surrendering allowances as required under Articles 3gb and 12 and for overall compliance with the provisions of national law transposing this Directive.»

**Penalty.** «The excess emissions penalty shall be EUR 100 for each tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent emitted for which the operator or aircraft operator has not surrendered allowances.» «The penalties set out in paragraph 3 shall also apply in respect of shipping companies.» «In the case of a shipping company that has failed to comply with the surrender obligations for two or more consecutive reporting periods, and where other enforcement measures have failed to ensure compliance, the competent authority of the Member State of the port of entry may, after giving the opportunity to the shipping company concerned to submit its observations, issue an expulsion order»

**Second system.** «Member States shall ensure that, from 1 January 2025, no regulated entity carries out the activity referred to in Annex III unless that regulated entity holds a permit issued by a competent authority» «From 1 January 2028, Member States shall ensure that, by 31 May each year, the regulated entity surrenders an amount of allowances covered by this Chapter that is equal to the regulated entity’s total emissions» «Where the average price of allowances referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article exceeds a price of EUR 45 for a period of two consecutive months, 20 million allowances covered by this Chapter shall be released from the market stability reserve» «From 1 January 2028, Member States shall ensure that, by 30 April each year until 2030, each regulated entity reports the average share of costs related to the surrender of allowances under this Chapter which it passed on to consumers for the preceding year.»

*Analytical inference:* every duty above falls on the shipping company, the regulated entity or Member States and the Commission; the Directive states a reimbursement route from the entity assuming responsibility for fuel or ship operation and a report by regulated entities on costs passed on, and it states no rate for the freight customer. It rests on the quoted cost transfer, penalty and reporting sentences. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a carrier's ETS charge to the workspace is a reimbursement under the cost transfer sentence or a separate commercial charge, and which penalty text governs a shipping company.

Obligations surveyed: 14; workspace-adjacent: 4; extracted as FACT: 14.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Monitoring plans: «Shipping companies will need to submit a monitoring plan for each of their ships falling within the scope of the MRV Maritime Regulation and the ETS Directive to their administering authority by 1 April 2024.» Registry accounts: «a shipping company shall submit to the relevant national administrator the information to request the opening of a Maritime Operator Holding Account». Reports for the second system: «Member States shall ensure that each regulated entity monitors for each calendar year from 2025 the emissions corresponding to the quantities of fuels released for consumption pursuant to Annex III.» «Member States shall ensure that, from 1 January 2025, no regulated entity carries out the activity referred to in Annex III unless that regulated entity holds a permit issued by a competent authority»

*Analytical inference:* the registration and reporting duties sit with shipping companies and regulated entities; the text states none on a party that books or arranges the cargo. It rests on the quoted sentences above. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a party that books or arranges cargo has any registration or reporting duty, since the quoted sentences attach to shipping companies and regulated entities.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

COST ALERT: the Directive builds no system for the workspace; the work is in the workspace's own rate and contract data. The system that exists is the carrier's: «the administering authority in respect of a shipping company shall ensure that a shipping company under its responsibility monitors and reports the relevant parameters».

- Carrier manager, at the next rate review: add to each ocean rate and contract record the name of the shipping company for the ship, whether an allowance cost is itemised, and the basis on which the carrier states it.
- Fuel buyer, at the next fuel supply renewal: add to each road transport fuel clause a field for the date from which the supplier's fuel price includes the second system's allowance cost, using the start year in section 6 until the Directive's 2027 or the reported 2028 is confirmed.
- Carrier manager, at the next rate review: close the gap that a rate sheet showing one all-in price per container or per kilometre cannot show an allowance component, by adding the question.

*Analytical inference:* these steps rest on the cost transfer and role sentences quoted in sections 3 and 4; the Directive does not require the workspace to keep these records. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether an itemised allowance charge in a carrier's quote can be audited against the shipping company's verified emissions, which the capture does not state.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Ice-class ships: «shipping companies may surrender 5 % fewer allowances than their verified emissions released until 31 December 2030 from ice-class ships» Container ships and transhipment ports: «The list established by the Commission pursuant to the first subparagraph shall not include ports located in a third country for which that third country effectively applies measures equivalent to this Directive.» Second system and national carbon taxes: «Until 31 December 2030, by way of derogation from paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article, where a regulated entity established in a given Member State is subject to a national carbon tax in force for the years 2027 to 2030». Smaller ships stay outside for now, as section 6 quotes.

*Analytical inference:* the ice-class allowance and the national carbon tax rule end on 31 December 2030 and apply only in the cases the sentences name; they do not change the 100 percent coverage that applies from 2026 for other ships. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular ship qualifies as an ice-class ship or a particular port as a neighbouring container transhipment port.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope

This document covers «COMMISSION DELEGATED REGULATION (EU) 2025/656 of 2 April 2025 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards standards for wireless recharging, electric road system, vehicle-to-grid communication and hydrogen supply for road transport vehicles». Its jurisdiction is the European Union: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» What the Regulation sets is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

*Analytical inference:* the amended instrument is Regulation (EU) 2023/1804, so this document is read with that text for the definitions and duties the annex serves, which the captured text does not reproduce.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Commission changes the technical standards for charging and hydrogen fuelling points: «Article 1 Annex II to Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 is amended in accordance with the Annex to this Regulation.» The reason it gives: «The Commission may amend Annex II on technical specifications of Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 to introduce new technical specifications or update references to the standards set out in that Annex to enable full technical interoperability of the recharging and refuelling infrastructure in terms of physical connections, communication exchanges and access for persons with reduced mobility.»

For heavy-duty electric vehicles the rule that matters is this: «Direct current (DC) high-power recharging points for recharging infrastructure capable of supplying electricity to both light- and heavy-duty electric vehicles shall be equipped, for interoperability purposes, at least with vehicle connectors of the combined charging system “Combo 2” for Mode 4 recharging as described in standard EN IEC 62196-3:2022» Hydrogen connectors for heavy-duty vehicles also change: «Technical specifications for connectors for refuelling points dispensing gaseous (compressed) hydrogen for heavy-duty vehicles shall comply, for interoperability purposes, at least with the requirements described in standard EN 17127:2024»

*Analytical inference:* an operator that moves freight on electric heavy-duty vehicles meets this Regulation as the connector and communication standard of the points those vehicles charge at; the date a point was installed or renovated decides which standard it was built to. The text states no cost for a freight operator.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no reader deadline falls in the next month; the Annex standards already apply to points installed or renovated from 8 January 2026, and the next dated step is the newer vehicle-to-grid standard: «installed or renovated from 1 January 2027 shall comply, for interoperability purposes, at least with standard EN ISO 15118-20:2022»

- A procurement lead, at the next tender or onboarding round and before 1 January 2027: asks the charging provider of each charging-dependent road lane whether any public point it will install or renovate from 1 January 2027 will support EN ISO 15118-20:2022.
- A procurement lead, before the business installs or renovates any private recharging point for its own heavy-duty electric vehicles from 1 January 2027: specifies EN ISO 15118-20:2022 for Mode 3 or Mode 4 in the purchase order, because the private rule has the same start date.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the install-or-renovate date in the span above; the text states no cost and no penalty. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business's own recharging points are private recharging points within the meaning of the Annex.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names the operators and manufacturers of recharging points. «Operators and manufacturers of both publicly accessible and private recharging points specifically for Mode 3 and 4 recharging for electric vehicles should prepare and predispose their hardware and software to properly support standard part EN ISO 15118-20:2022 from 1 January 2027 in all newly installed or renovated recharging points.» A forwarder is not named, and neither is a carrier or a shipper. The cybersecurity rules of another directive sit beside this Regulation: «As Directive (EU) 2022/2555 includes operators of recharging points as part of a sector of high criticality, the application of that Directive and the requirements set out in Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 should be complementary.»

*Analytical inference:* a freight business meets the Regulation as a user of public points, or as the owner of private points if it installs its own; the duties in the text fall on the operators and manufacturers it names. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business that installs private recharging points counts as an operator in the sense of the Annex.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

One standard is still to come. The Commission records that the megawatt charging system rules are not yet part of the Annex: «that standard should not apply to recharging infrastructure dedicated exclusively to heavy-duty vehicles and equipped solely with the MCS, as the relevant technical specifications will be introduced in Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 once the standardisation work for the MCS is completed» The captured text gives no date for the megawatt charging system standard.

*Analytical inference:* until that standard is added, infrastructure built only for the megawatt charging system sits outside the Combo 2 connector rule in section 8, so a heavy-duty electric vehicle fleet cannot assume that every future high-power point will carry the connector this Regulation names. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the recital's statement that the standard "should not apply" to megawatt-only infrastructure operates as a binding exclusion or only as an explanation of the Annex text.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Which standard a point follows depends on whether it is installed or renovated from the stated date. The Annex defines both words: «“installed” means the initial placement of all relevant recharging point equipment, including hardware, software and associated electrical infrastructure, such as electricity supply connections, transformers, and other electrical systems, to enable the recharging of electric vehicles» and «“renovated” means a major or complete replacement of relevant recharging point equipment» The recitals add: «Regular maintenance updates, including the replacement of specific components, such as recharging cables should not be considered as renovation.»

*Analytical inference:* a cable replacement does not move a point to the new standard, while a major replacement of its equipment does. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular upgrade of an existing point is a renovation in the sense of the Annex.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Light-duty points from 8 January 2026. «alternating current (AC) normal-power recharging points for light-duty electric vehicles installed or renovated from 8 January 2026 shall be equipped, for interoperability purposes, at least with socket-outlets or vehicle connectors of Type 2 for Mode 3 recharging as described in standard EN IEC 62196-2:2022»

Heavy-duty points. «Direct current (DC) high-power recharging points for recharging infrastructure capable of supplying electricity to both light- and heavy-duty electric vehicles shall be equipped, for interoperability purposes, at least with vehicle connectors of the combined charging system “Combo 2” for Mode 4 recharging as described in standard EN IEC 62196-3:2022»

Wireless and road-fed power. «Recharging points for light-duty electric vehicles dedicated to inductive static wireless recharging shall comply, for interoperability purposes, with: — EN IEC 61980-1:2021» «Recharging infrastructure for alternating current (AC) and direct current (DC) dedicated to electric road system (ERS) for dynamic ground-level power supply through conductive rails for light- and heavy-duty electric vehicles equipped with ground level current collector devices, to enable conductive current collection by road vehicles from a feeding track integrated in the roadway shall comply, for interoperability purposes, with: — CLC/TS 50717:2022»

Vehicle-to-grid communication from 8 January 2026. «The publicly accessible recharging points for alternating current (AC) and direct current (DC) for light- and heavy-duty electric vehicles installed or renovated from 8 January 2026 shall comply, for interoperability purposes, at least with the following standards: — EN ISO 15118-1:2019 “Road vehicles – Vehicle to grid communication interface Part 1: General information and use-case definition”; — EN ISO 15118-2:2016» From 1 January 2027. «Publicly accessible recharging points for alternating current (AC) and direct current (DC) for light- and heavy-duty electric vehicles installed or renovated from 1 January 2027 shall comply, for interoperability purposes, at least with standard EN ISO 15118-20:2022» Private points. «Private recharging points for alternating current (AC) and direct current (DC) electric light- and heavy-duty electric vehicles installed or renovated from 1 January 2027 shall comply, for interoperability purposes, at least with the following standards: (a) EN IEC 61851-1:2019 “Electric vehicle conductive charging system – Part 1: General requirements” (for Mode 2 recharging); (b) EN ISO 15118-20:2022 “Road vehicles – Vehicle to grid communication interface – Part 20: 2nd generation network layer and application layer requirements” (for Mode 3 or Mode 4 recharging)»

Existing points. «existing publicly accessible recharging points for Mode 3 and 4 recharging using low-level communication such as PWM, which are already capable of communicating with electric vehicles on the market equipped with EN ISO 15118-2:2016, should be exempted from implementing Parts 1 to 5 of standard EN ISO 15118» Scope by vehicle category. «The amendments to the titles and scope of points 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 of Annex II to Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 are necessary to achieve a clearer presentation of the standards applicable for each vehicle category.»

Penalty. The captured text states no penalty, fine or sanction and no enforcement consequence; enforcement of the parent Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 is not in the captured text.

*Analytical inference:* the cause is a technical standard in an annex; the mechanical consequence is that a point installed or renovated from the stated date carries the connector and communication standard named; the effect for a freight business that charges heavy-duty electric vehicles is compatibility between its vehicles and those points. The text does not state how any cost reaches a rate. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which party is the duty holder for each standard, and whether Member State law adds a penalty.

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 4; extracted as FACT: 9.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The captured text states no registration or reporting duty. The Regulation sets technical standards for points and states no registration scheme.

*Analytical inference:* the only information a freight business would collect is the install-or-renovate date and the supported standard of the points it relies on.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the system work in the text falls on the operators and manufacturers of recharging points, not on a freight business. The recital that sets the expectation: «Operators and manufacturers of both publicly accessible and private recharging points specifically for Mode 3 and 4 recharging for electric vehicles should prepare and predispose their hardware and software to properly support standard part EN ISO 15118-20:2022 from 1 January 2027 in all newly installed or renovated recharging points.»

- A procurement lead, at each carrier or charging-provider record update before 1 January 2027: adds the install-or-renovate date and the vehicle-to-grid standard as two fields.

*Operational implication:* the two fields let the business tell which standard a point it relies on was built to. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any of this reaches the business as a duty rather than as a supplier question.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Older points are protected from replacement. For private Mode 2 points: «for existing private recharging points for Mode 2 recharging, using low-level communication solutions such as PWM, that are already capable of covering basic recharging functions with normal household sockets and communicate with electric vehicles on the market equipped with EN ISO 15118-2:2016 should also be exempted from implementing Parts 1 to 5 of standard EN ISO 15118»

*Analytical inference:* a freight business that charges at an older point may find it follows the earlier standard until it is renovated. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given older point qualifies for the exemption.

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 2 April 2025: adopted. «Done at Brussels, 2 April 2025.»
- 18 June 2025: published in the Official Journal. «L series 2025/656 18.6.2025»
- 8 January 2026: the Regulation applies; points installed or renovated from this date follow the Annex II standards as replaced (date passed). «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . It shall apply from 8 January 2026.»
- 1 January 2027: public and private points installed or renovated from this date follow the newer vehicle-to-grid standard. «installed or renovated from 1 January 2027 shall comply, for interoperability purposes, at least with standard EN ISO 15118-20:2022»

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2023/956 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 10 May 2023 establishing a carbon border adjustment mechanism», the European Union's carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM). The 2023 text has since been amended: «Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 , published on 17 October following adoption by the Council, amends Regulation (EU) 2023/956 of 10 May 2023 that introduced the EU CBAM». The text of Regulation 2025/2083 is not among the pages held; the amended values below come from the Commission portal and from ICAP, an industry body, and are named as such. Where the 2023 text and the later description differ, this document follows the later description and says so. What the Regulation requires is stated from its own words; what it means for the workspace is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

Its reach: «This Regulation applies to goods listed in Annex I originating in a third country, where those goods, or processed products from those goods resulting from the inward processing procedure referred to in Article 256 of Regulation (EU) No 952/2013, are imported into the customs territory of the Union.»

It enters into force as its final article states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union»

*Analytical inference:* the jurisdiction is the customs territory of the Union, so the mechanism attaches at import into that territory, wherever the goods were made. It rests on the sentence on scope quoted above.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

«The Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) is the EU's tool to put a fair price on carbon emitted during the production of carbon-intensive goods that are entering the EU, and to encourage cleaner industrial production in non-EU countries.» The goods it covers: «CBAM will initially apply to imports of certain goods and selected precursors whose production is carbon-intensive and at most significant risk of carbon leakage: cement, iron and steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen». The cost is paid in certificates: «The price of the certificates will be calculated based on auction price of EU ETS allowances», «as a quarterly average in 2026 and as a weekly average from 2027 onwards.» Only one kind of party may bring the goods in: «Goods shall be imported into the customs territory of the Union only by an authorised CBAM declarant.»

Why it applies to the workspace: any customs declaration the workspace lodges, or any import it arranges for a client, may concern goods in the listed groups, and the party named on that import carries the declarant duties. The text held here does not say how a declarant charges the cost of certificates to the owner of the goods.

*Analytical inference:* the workspace is affected when it lodges customs declarations for cement, iron and steel, aluminium, fertiliser, electricity or hydrogen imports, because the duty to hold authorised status attaches to the importer or its indirect customs representative (the application sentences in section 4). It rests on the declarant sentence and the list of covered goods quoted above.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

COST ALERT: the definitive period is in force and the certificate cost is now a priced item. The Commission's own page puts the first declaration and surrender at «By 30 September 2027, importers of CBAM goods must submit their first CBAM declaration and surrender the corresponding CBAM certificates.» The industry body ICAP reports, in its description of Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 (the amending text itself is not among the pages held), that certificate sales open later than first planned: «The start of CBAM certificates sales is postponed from 1 January 2026 to 1 February 2027.»

- Customs desk lead, by the first import of each quarter: sort every import by whether the goods are in the listed groups and whether the importer's yearly total passes the threshold in «single mass-based threshold of 50 tonnes of CBAM goods», and record for each import the party that is importer and the party that would apply for authorised declarant status.
- Account manager, at the next rate review with each importer of covered goods: ask whether it holds, or has applied for, authorised declarant status, and who it has named to lodge the declaration; ICAP, an industry body, describes the delegation rule: «Authorized CBAM declarants may delegate submission of CBAM declarations to a third party, while retaining responsibility.»
- Pricing lead, before the first quote for covered goods after certificate sales open: put a line in each quote that states who buys the certificates and on what price basis, because the Commission portal says the price basis changes after the first year: «as a quarterly average in 2026 and as a weekly average from 2027 onwards.»

*Analytical inference:* each step rests on the quoted import, threshold and declarant sentences; the texts held state no fixed price per certificate and no rule on how a declarant charges the owner of the goods. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace, when it lodges a customs declaration for a client, is the importer or an indirect customs representative for these goods, and who bears the declarant duties in each case.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names these roles. The importer: «‘importer’ means either the person lodging a customs declaration for release for free circulation of goods in its own name and on its own behalf or, where the customs declaration is lodged by an indirect customs representative in accordance with Article 18 of Regulation (EU) No 952/2013, the person on whose behalf such a declaration is lodged;» The importer applies first: «Any importer established in a Member State shall, prior to importing goods into the customs territory of the Union, apply for the status of authorised CBAM declarant (‘application for an authorisation’). Where such an importer appoints an indirect customs representative in accordance with Article 18 of Regulation (EU) No 952/2013 and the indirect customs representative agrees to act as an authorised CBAM declarant, the indirect customs representative shall submit the application for an authorisation.» Where the importer is outside the Member States: «Where an importer is not established in a Member State, the indirect customs representative shall submit the application for an authorisation.» The competent authority is defined as «‘competent authority’ means the authority designated by each Member State in accordance with Article 11;» and customs authorities as «‘customs authorities’ means the customs administrations of Member States». A forwarder is not named in the text held here; the roles that can fall to a customs agent are the indirect customs representative and the third party that lodges a declaration for a declarant.

*Analytical inference:* where the workspace lodges a customs declaration for another person's goods, it sits in the indirect customs representative position described above, and it becomes the declarant only if it agrees to act as one. It rests on the application sentences quoted above. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which role the workspace holds for each import, and whether a given arrangement counts as the appointment of an indirect customs representative under the Union Customs Code article the Regulation cites.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

Dated steps and open reviews at the date of this document.

- The Commission report on the transitional period: «Before the end of the transitional period referred to in Article 32, the Commission shall present a report to the European Parliament and to the Council on the application of this Regulation.» The transitional period has ended; the Commission's legislation page lists a «Report on the application of the CBAM Regulation».
- A widening of scope is in train: «The European Commission welcomes the Council agreement to extend the CBAM to specific downstream goods and reinforce existing anti-circumvention safeguards.» The capture does not say when it would apply.
- A consultation on carbon price paid abroad has closed: «On 13 May 2026, the Commission published the implementing act for a 4-week public consultation ending on 10 June 2026.»
- Default carbon prices are still to come: «From 2027, the Commission will publish default carbon prices and related calculation methodologies in the CBAM registry.»
- A deadline for an implementing act on indirect emissions has passed: «The Commission shall adopt, no later than 30 June 2025, an implementing act pursuant to Article 7(7)». The capture does not say that it was adopted by that date.
- Electricity from coupled third countries: «the first report by 1 July 2025 and the second by 31 December 2027. By 31 December 2025 and by 1 July 2028, the Commission shall assess».
- Scope growth timetable: «a timetable ending in 2030 for the gradual inclusion of the goods within the scope of this Regulation».

*Analytical inference:* the downstream goods step and the carbon price paid abroad act each concern a declarant's calculation; the capture gives no date for either and states no effect. They rest on the Council agreement sentence and the consultation sentence quoted above.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

**Scope.** «This Regulation applies to goods listed in Annex I originating in a third country, where those goods, or processed products from those goods resulting from the inward processing procedure referred to in Article 256 of Regulation (EU) No 952/2013, are imported into the customs territory of the Union.»

**Declarant declaration.** «The CBAM declaration shall contain the following information: (a) the total quantity of each type of goods imported during the preceding calendar year, expressed in megawatt-hours for electricity and in tonnes for other goods; (b) the total embedded emissions in the goods referred to in point (a) of this paragraph, expressed in tonnes of CO 2 e emissions per megawatt-hour of electricity or, for other goods, in tonnes of CO 2 e emissions per tonne of each type of goods, calculated in accordance with Article 7 and verified in accordance with Article 8; (c) the total number of CBAM certificates to be surrendered, corresponding to the total embedded emissions referred to in point (b) of this paragraph after the reduction that is due on the account of the carbon price paid in a country of origin in accordance with Article 9 and the adjustment necessary to reflect the extent to which EU ETS allowances are allocated free of charge in accordance with Article 31; (d) copies of verification reports, issued by accredited verifiers, under Article 8 and Annex VI.»

**Declaration timing, as amended (ICAP's description).** «The submission deadline for the annual CBAM declaration is postponed to 30 September (previously 31 May) of the year following importation of covered goods.»

**Surrender and holding (ICAP's description).** «the requirement for declarants to hold a number of CBAM certificates on their registry account at the end of each quarter is reduced to 50% of embedded emissions in goods imported since the beginning of the calendar year (down from 80%).»

**Price (the 2023 text; ICAP for 2026).** «The Commission shall calculate the price of CBAM certificates as the average of the closing prices of EU ETS allowances on the auction platform, in accordance with the procedures laid down in Regulation (EU) No 1031/2010, for each calendar week.» «Certificates prices for the 2026 compliance year will reflect the quarterly average of 2026 EU ETS allowance prices.»

**Free allocation adjustment (the 2023 text; ICAP for the 2026 to 2034 phase-out).** «The CBAM certificates to be surrendered in accordance with Article 22 of this Regulation shall be adjusted to reflect the extent to which EU ETS allowances are allocated free of charge in accordance with Article 10a of Directive 2003/87/EC to installations producing, within the Union, the goods listed in Annex I to this Regulation.» «the gradual phase-out of free allocation for CBAM-covered sectors in the EU ETS from 2026 to 2034»

**Carbon price paid abroad (ICAP's description).** «Standard annual average carbon prices, or default carbon prices, may be used for countries where carbon pricing mechanisms are in place, but an actual carbon price paid cannot be established.»

**Exempt volume (ICAP's description).** «A new single mass-based threshold exempts importers that bring in 50 tons or less»

**Penalty.** «Such a penalty shall be identical to the excess emissions penalty set out in Article 16(3) of Directive 2003/87/EC and increased pursuant to Article 16(4) of that Directive, applicable in the year of importation of the goods. Such a penalty shall apply for each CBAM certificate that the authorised CBAM declarant has not surrendered.» A person who is not a declarant is also reached: «that person shall be held liable for the payment of a penalty.»

*Analytical inference:* the surrender duty, the quarterly holding duty and the penalty fall on the authorised declarant; the text held here states no cost to the owner of the goods and does not name a forwarder. It rests on the penalty and surrender sentences above. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any of these duties can be contractually moved to the owner of the goods or to the workspace, and which version of each date applies to a given import.
