## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Applying for status goes through the registry: «The application for an authorisation shall be submitted via the CBAM registry established in accordance with Article 14.» Who gets access: «Access to the CBAM registry should be requested through the National Competent Authority (NCA) of the EU country in which the importer is established.» Who must apply: «EU importers or their indirect customs representatives importing more than the single mass-based threshold of 50 tonnes of CBAM goods into the EU will have to apply for the status of authorized CBAM declarants.». Reporting under the transitional period ended: «The last CBAM report, which is the report to be submitted for the last quarter of 2025, should be submitted by 31 January 2026.»

*Analytical inference:* the registration and reporting duties sit with the importer or its indirect customs representative; the text states none on a party that only moves the goods. It rests on the application sentences quoted above. *Legal Confirmation Required:* who must register when the workspace lodges the customs declaration on a client's behalf.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

COST ALERT: the system work sits with whoever is declarant, and the workspace can be asked to supply the data. What a declarant must hold and file: «(a) the total quantity of each type of goods imported during the preceding calendar year, expressed in megawatt-hours for electricity and in tonnes for other goods;» Where producers' data is missing: «Default emission values are introduced for countries lacking reliable data.» Importers also need an account in the registry: «need a CBAM account number or application reference number». Verification has its own rules: «This new page contains information on CBAM verification rules and the accreditation framework for verifiers.»

- Operations lead, by the first import of covered goods each month: add to the import file a record of the mass in tonnes (megawatt-hours for electricity), the importer's registry account number or application reference, and the producer's emissions data or the fact that a default value is used.
- Account manager, before the start of certificate sales on 1 February 2027: agree in writing with each importer of covered goods who submits the declaration, who buys the certificates and who bears the cost if a default value is replaced by an actual value.
- Systems owner, by 30 September 2027: close the gap that import files holding quantity and value but no emissions data cannot support a declaration, by building the emissions field and the supplier data request.

*Analytical inference:* each step follows from the declaration contents and the default value sentence quoted above; the texts held do not require the workspace itself to file anything unless it acts as declarant. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a contract with a client that moves the cost or data duties to the workspace is valid under the Regulation.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

The 2023 text sets one exclusion by origin: «By way of derogation from paragraphs 1 and 2, this Regulation shall not apply to goods originating in the third countries and territories listed in point 1 of Annex III.» The industry body ICAP reports a volume exemption: «A new single mass-based threshold exempts importers that bring in 50 tons or less», and the Commission describes its reach: «the new threshold exempts 90% of importers while still covering 99% of embedded emissions from CBAM-covered goods imported into the EU». The same page limits that exemption: «Hydrogen and electricity are excluded from this» exemption. Electricity from coupled third countries has a time-limited rule: «third countries whose markets are coupled with that of the Union should benefit from a time-limited exemption from the CBAM until 2030 with regard solely to the export of electricity, provided that certain conditions are met.»

*Analytical inference:* an importer under the yearly volume can bring covered goods in without declarant status, but hydrogen and electricity imports cannot use that exemption. It rests on the volume and exclusion sentences quoted above. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular import falls under the origin exclusion in the 2023 text, which the capture does not show amended, and how the volume is counted for the importer concerned.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope

This document covers «DIRECTIVE (EU) 2025/1892 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 10 September 2025 amending Directive 2008/98/EC on waste». It is addressed to the Member States: «This Directive is addressed to the Member States.» What the Directive sets is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

*Analytical inference:* the Directive reaches businesses only through national laws that the Member States write by the date in section 3, so every duty below is a duty on Member States to ensure something, and the national text decides who is bound.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Directive changes the EU waste law in two parts: national food waste reduction targets, and extended producer responsibility for textiles, clothing accessories and footwear. The products in scope are set by tariff code in the Annex: «ANNEX IVc PRODUCTS THAT FALL WITHIN THE SCOPE OF THE EXTENDED PRODUCER RESPONSIBILITY FOR CERTAIN TEXTILE, TEXTILE-RELATED AND FOOTWEAR PRODUCTS» Examples are «6309 Worn clothing and other worn articles» and «6403 Footwear with outer soles of rubber, plastics, leather or composition leather and uppers of leather»

Entry into force: «This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union» A recital records the import share of this market: «73 % of clothes and household textiles consumed in Europe are imported»

*Analytical inference:* the import share suggests that the import flows of listed clothing, textiles and footwear are the flows on which a producer is registered and charged, so the cost lands first on the party that is the producer in each Member State of first supply, and may reach transport clients through national rules the text does not hold. The text states no cost figure.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no reader deadline falls in the next month; the dates in the text are Member State and Commission steps. The transposition date is: «Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 17 June 2027 at the latest.» The schemes are due: «Member States shall ensure that the extended producer responsibility schemes laid down in paragraph 1 of this Article are established by 17 April 2028 in accordance with Articles 8, 8a, and 22a to 22d.»

- A client-relations lead, at the next account review and before 17 June 2027: asks each client that imports or distance-sells clothing, textiles or footwear into the Union whether it will be the producer in each Member State of first supply, and who will register it.
- A documentation lead, before the next shipment of used clothing, textiles or footwear for re-use: checks the papers against the invoice, bale record and declaration list in section 8.
- A contracts lead, at the next contract renewal with an online seller of these goods and before 17 April 2028: notes which warehouse or order-handling services the business sells, and asks counsel whether any of them make it a fulfilment service provider.

*Analytical inference:* the three steps rest on the producer definition in section 7, the shipment documents in section 8 and the fulfilment duties in section 8; no cost is stated. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business or its clients fall in those definitions in each Member State.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Directive names producers, authorised representatives, producer responsibility organisations, online platforms, fulfilment service providers, social economy entities, the Commission, Member States and their competent authorities. A forwarder is not named. Three places touch the work of a freight business.

Authorised representative for a distance seller: «Member States shall ensure that a producer as defined in Article 3(4b), point (d), established in another Member State and making textile, textile-related or footwear products listed in Annex IVc available for the first time on their territory appoints, by written mandate, a legal or natural person established on their territory as its authorised representative for the purpose of fulfilling the obligations of a producer related to the extended producer responsibility scheme on their territory.»

Fulfilment service providers: «“fulfilment service provider” means fulfilment service provider as defined in Article 3, point (11), of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020»

Transport of used textiles: «a declaration made by the natural or legal person in possession of used textile, textile-related or footwear products assessed as fit for re-use that arranges, on a professional basis, the transport of used textile, textile-related and footwear products assessed as fit for re-use that none of the material within the consignment is waste as defined by Article 3(1).»

*Analytical inference:* a freight business is in the chain only where it is itself the producer, a fulfilment service provider, or the natural or legal person in possession of used goods assessed as fit for re-use that arranges their transport on a professional basis. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which of these roles, if any, the business holds for each client and lane.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

Several acts are still to come. Registration format: «By 17 April 2027, the Commission shall adopt implementing acts establishing the harmonised format for registration in the register of producers» Delegated acts: «The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 22a(5) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 17 April 2027.» Food waste correction factor: «by 17 October 2027, the Commission shall adopt implementing acts establishing a correction factor to account for the increase or decrease in tourism» Review of the food waste targets: «By 31 December 2027, the Commission shall review the targets to be reached by 2030, laid down in paragraph 4» That review is to include an assessment of binding targets for 2035: «an assessment of the possibility to introduce legally binding targets with respect to paragraph 4, points (a) and (b), to be reached by 2035» Evaluation of the Directive: «By 31 December 2029, the Commission shall evaluate this Directive and Directive 1999/31/EC.»

*Analytical inference:* the registration format due on the first date decides what a producer, or an authorised representative, files in each Member State; the text states no date for the national registers themselves.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Whether a business is a producer decides everything else. The definition: «“producer of textile, textile-related or footwear products listed in Annex IVc” means any manufacturer, importer or distributor or other natural or legal person, that, irrespective of the selling technique used» Importers: «(c) is established in a Member State and supplies for the first time within the territory of that Member State on a professional basis, textile, textile-related or footwear products listed in Annex IVc from another Member State or from a third country» Distance sellers: «(d) sells textile, textile-related or footwear products listed in Annex IVc by means of distance contracts directly to end-users, whether or not they are private households, in a Member State, and is established in another Member State or in a third country.» Excluded: «“producer of textile, textile-related or footwear products listed in Annex IVc” does not include manufacturers, importers or distributors or other natural or legal persons that supply used textile, textile-related or footwear products listed in Annex IVc assessed as fit for re-use»

For fulfilment service providers: The captured text does not define the services that make a business a fulfilment service provider; the definition sits in Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, which is not in the captured text.

*Analytical inference:* an importer that supplies listed goods for the first time in a Member State, and a distance seller established elsewhere, are producers in the sense of the text; a business that only carries the goods is not stated to be one. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a business that clears goods in its own name is a producer for the first supply.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Producer responsibility. «Member States shall ensure that producers have extended producer responsibility for textile, textile-related or footwear products listed in Annex IVc that they make available on the market for the first time, in accordance with Articles 8 and 8a.»

Costs. «Member States shall ensure that the producers of textile, textile-related or footwear products listed in Annex IVc cover the costs of the following: (a) collection of used and waste textile, textile-related and footwear products listed in Annex IVc and subsequent waste management» Fees: «Member States shall require producer responsibility organisations to ensure that the financial contributions paid to them by producers of textile, textile-related or footwear products listed in Annex IVc: (a) are based on the weight and, where appropriate, the quantity of the products concerned»

Producer responsibility organisations. «Member States shall ensure that producers of textile, textile-related or footwear products listed in Annex IVc entrust a producer responsibility organisation to fulfil their extended producer responsibility obligations laid down in Article 22a on their behalf.»

Registration. «Member States shall only allow producers to make available on the market for the first time textile, textile-related or footwear products listed in Annex IVc where they or, in the case of authorisation, their authorised representatives for extended producer responsibility, are registered in the Member State in question.»

Online platforms. «Member States shall ensure that providers of online platforms falling within the scope of Chapter III, Section 4, of that Regulation that allow consumers to conclude distance contracts with producers offering textile, textile-related or footwear products listed in Annex IVc to consumers located in the Union obtain the following information from producers prior to allowing them to use their services»

Fulfilment service providers. «Member States shall adopt measures to ensure that producers offering textile, textile-related or footwear products listed in Annex IVc to end users located in the Union provide fulfilment service providers with the information referred to in paragraph 13» «Member States shall ensure that the fulfilment service provider, upon receiving the information referred to in paragraph 15 and at the moment of the conclusion of the contract between the fulfilment service provider and the producer for any of the services referred to in Article 3, point (11), of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, through the use of any freely accessible official online database or online interface made available by a Member State or the Union or through requests to the producer to provide supporting documents from reliable sources, makes best efforts to assess whether the information referred to in paragraph 15 of this Article is reliable and complete.» «where the producer fails to correct, complete or update that information, the fulfilment service provider swiftly suspends the provision of its service to that producer»

Sorting. «Member States shall ensure that used and waste textile, textile-related and footwear products that are separately collected, including in accordance with Article 22c(8) and (11), are subject to sorting operations to ensure the treatment in line with the waste hierarchy.»

Shipments of used goods for re-use. «Member States shall ensure that shipments arranged on a professional basis of used textile, textile-related and footwear products assessed as fit for re-use comply with the minimum record-keeping requirements set out in paragraph 9 and are accompanied by at least the following information» «(a) a copy of the invoice and contract relating to the sale or transfer of ownership of the textiles, textile-related and footwear products which states that they are destined for direct re-use and that they are fit for direct re-use» The bale record: «in the form of a copy of the records on every bale within the consignment» The declaration: «a declaration made by the natural or legal person in possession of used textile, textile-related or footwear products assessed as fit for re-use that arranges, on a professional basis, the transport of used textile, textile-related and footwear products assessed as fit for re-use that none of the material within the consignment is waste as defined by Article 3(1).» Packing: «are appropriately protected against damage during transportation, loading and unloading, in particular, through sufficient packaging and appropriate stacking of the load» Inspection: «shipments of used textile, textile-related and footwear products assessed as fit for re-use suspected of being waste may be inspected by the competent authorities of Member States» Costs of inspection: «the costs of appropriate analyses, inspections and storage of used textile, textile-related or footwear products assessed as fit for re-use suspected of being waste may be charged to the producers of textile, textile-related or footwear products listed in Annex IVc, to third parties acting on their behalf or to other persons arranging the shipment»

Food waste. «Member States shall take the necessary and appropriate measures to achieve, by 31 December 2030, the following food waste reduction targets at national level: (a) reduction of the generation of food waste in processing and manufacturing by 10 % in comparison to the amount of food waste generated as an annual average between 2021 and 2023»

Penalty. The enforcement consequence the text states is the refusal or withdrawal of a producer's registration, quoted in section 10. The captured text states no fine or fee amount; penalties and fee levels sit in national law, which is not in the captured text.

*Analytical inference:* the cause is the producer definition; the mechanical consequence is that a producer in a Member State pays for collection and sorting, based on weight, through a producer responsibility organisation, and cannot place goods on that market for the first time without being registered; the effect for a freight business is on the importer and distance-seller clients and on any shipment of used goods for re-use. The text does not state how any fee reaches a freight rate. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which party is the producer for a given import, and whether the shipment documents apply to the business's exports of used goods.

No phase-in is stated beyond the dates in section 14.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Producers register in each Member State where they first make listed goods available: «Member States shall ensure that producers are required to register in the register of producers. To that end, Member States shall require the producers to submit an application for registration in each Member State where they make available textile, textile-related or footwear products listed in Annex IVc on the market for the first time.» The authority grants registration: «grants registrations and provides a registration number within a maximum period of 12 weeks from the date that the information laid down in paragraph 4 is provided» The enforcement consequence the text states is that the authority can refuse or withdraw registration: «The competent authority may refuse or withdraw the producer’s registration where the information laid down in paragraph 4 and related documentary evidence is not provided or is insufficient» Producer responsibility organisations report each year: «Member States shall ensure that producer responsibility organisations provide, on an annual basis, the competent authorities with the information referred to in paragraph 18, points (a) and (b)» A smaller producer reports less: «By way of derogation from the first subparagraph of this paragraph, Member States shall require that, in respect of producers that are enterprises that employ fewer than 10 persons and whose annual turnover and annual balance sheet does not exceed EUR 2 million, producer responsibility organisations request those enterprises to submit, on an annual basis, only the information listed in paragraph 18, point (a), point (i).»

*Analytical inference:* the register is the access point for online platforms and fulfilment service providers; the registration format is still to be adopted (section 6).

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the system work in the text falls on producers, their organisations and Member States. For a freight business the operational points are the shipment papers and the producer data it may be asked to check: «Member States shall adopt measures to ensure that producers offering textile, textile-related or footwear products listed in Annex IVc to end users located in the Union provide fulfilment service providers with the information referred to in paragraph 13»

- A documentation lead, at each consignment of used goods for re-use: keeps the invoice, bale record and declaration with the consignment.
- A contracts lead, at each new online-seller client and before 17 April 2028: if the business is a fulfilment service provider, records the registration number and self-certification the client gives it.

*Operational implication:* a business that serves online sellers of listed goods holds the registration number and self-certification each client gives it, if it is a fulfilment service provider; a business that ships used goods for re-use holds the invoice, bale record and declaration for each consignment. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether these records are the business's own duty or the client's.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Goods handed over directly for re-use are not considered waste upon collection: «used textile, textile-related and footwear products that are directly handed over by end users and directly professionally assessed as fit for re-use at the collection point by the re-use operator or social economy entities shall not be considered to be waste upon collection» Social economy entities may be relieved of reporting: «Member States may exempt, partially or totally, social economy entities from the obligation to submit the information in paragraph 12» Small enterprises come in later: «From 17 April 2029, Articles 22a, 22b, 22c and 22d shall apply to enterprises which employ fewer than 10 persons and whose annual turnover and annual balance sheet does not exceed EUR 2 million.» Cost cover has a date: where a Member State already had a scheme on 16 October 2025, producers cover the collection and sorting costs for goods first made available from that date: «were made available on the market for the first time from 16 October 2025 if an extended producer responsibility scheme for textile, textile-related and footwear products listed in Annex IVc is already established in the Member State in question»

*Analytical inference:* an exemption depends on the national law that applies it. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given hand-over or entity qualifies in the Member State concerned.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «Directive (EU) 2019/1161 of the European Parliament and of the Council», dated «of 20 June 2019» and titled in part «amending Directive 2009/33/EC on the promotion of clean and energy-efficient road transport vehicles». Its jurisdiction is the European Union, and it speaks to governments, not to companies. The jurisdictional scope is stated in its last article: «This Directive is addressed to the Member States.» It changes how public buyers choose road vehicles and road transport services.

What the Directive says is taken from its own text. What it may mean for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Directive rewrites the main rules of the earlier clean-vehicle procurement directive. Its stated aim: «This Directive requires Member States to ensure that contracting authorities and contracting entities take into account lifetime energy and environmental impacts, including energy consumption» and the rest of the sentence adds «and of certain pollutants, when procuring certain road transport vehicles with the objectives of promoting and stimulating the market for clean and energy-efficient vehicles and of improving the contribution of the transport sector to the environment, climate and energy policies of the Union.»

The reach of the Directive is set by the kind of contract. It covers «service contracts set out in Table 1 of the Annex to this Directive in so far as the contracting authorities or contracting entities are under an obligation to apply the procurement procedures set out in Directives 2014/24/EU and 2014/25/EU.» Table 1 lists road services that a freight business can meet in public tenders: «Mail transport by road», «Parcel transport services», «Parcel delivery services» and «refuse collection services». The recitals give the reason for including services: «Extending the scope of Directive 2009/33/EC by including practices such as lease, rental and hire-purchase of vehicles, as well as contracts for certain services, ensures that all relevant procurement practices are covered.»

*Analytical inference:* a freight business meets this Directive as a supplier to a public buyer. The buyer's contract is what the Directive reaches, and the quoted articles name no duty on a supplier.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no deadline of this Directive falls on a freight business inside the next 30 days, and the Directive states no cost for a supplier. The next dated step is the Commission's report: «By 18 April 2027, and every three years thereafter, the Commission shall submit a report to the European Parliament and to the Council on the implementation of this Directive».

- A public tenders lead reads the vehicle and fuel conditions of each public tender for road transport of mail, parcels or refuse collection before the next bid is priced, and records whether the buyer asks for clean or zero-emission vehicles.
- A pricing lead adds a line to the public-tender quote sheet for any vehicle or fuel condition a buyer sets, and fills it from the tender documents on the next public quote.

The reason is the counting rule: «In the case of contracts referred to in points (b) and (c) of Article 3(1), the number of road transport vehicles to be used for the provision of the services covered by each contract shall be taken into account for the purpose of assessing compliance with the minimum procurement targets.»

*Analytical inference:* the vehicles used on a covered service contract count toward the Member State's target, so a buyer has a reason to ask a bidder what vehicles it will use. The quoted rule states no question to bidders. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the national law that carries this Directive into force puts a vehicle or fuel condition on suppliers of a service contract.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Directive names buyers, States and the Commission. Buyers are defined by reference to the public procurement directives: «“contracting authorities” means contracting authorities as defined in point 1 of Article 2(1) of Directive 2014/24/EU and in Article 3 of Directive 2014/25/EU;» and «“contracting entities” means contracting entities as defined in Article 4 of Directive 2014/25/EU;». The Commission has a supporting role: «The Commission shall facilitate and structure the exchange of knowledge and best practices between Member States on practices for promoting procurement of clean and energy-efficient road transport vehicles by contracting authorities and contracting entities.» A forwarder is not named as a party.

The recitals show how a buyer can pass a condition down: «Where liquid biofuels, synthetic or paraffinic fuels are to be used by procured vehicles, contracting authorities and contracting entities have to ensure, through mandatory contract clauses or through similarly effective means within the public procurement procedure, that only such fuels are to be used in those vehicles.»

*Analytical inference:* a freight business sits below the Directive's chain. Member States answer for the targets, public buyers carry them through tenders, and the business meets them as a bidder or contractor under the contract clauses a buyer chooses. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given customer is a contracting authority or contracting entity under national law, and whether a contract clause on vehicle fuel binds the business that performs the service.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Directive sets its own dated follow-up steps. The Commission reports on implementation: «By 18 April 2027, and every three years thereafter, the Commission shall submit a report to the European Parliament and to the Council on the implementation of this Directive, specifying the measures taken by Member States in this regard, following the reports referred to in paragraph 2.» It then reviews the whole Directive: «By 31 December 2027, the Commission shall review the implementation of this Directive and, where appropriate, submit a legislative proposal for its amendment for the period after 2030, including for the setting of new targets and for the inclusion of other categories of vehicles, such as two- and three-wheeled vehicles.» A report format is still to be set: «The Commission shall adopt implementing acts in accordance with Article 9(2) setting out the format of the reports referred to in paragraph 2 of this Article and their transmission arrangements.» The text gives no date for that implementing act.

*Analytical inference:* the review due on 31 December 2027 is the point at which new targets after 2030 and further vehicle categories could be proposed. The text states no content for any such proposal, so nothing about a later rule can be planned from it. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the Commission has since adopted the implementing act on report format.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The first question is which vehicles are counted. The Directive defines them: «“road transport vehicle” means a vehicle of category M or N, as defined in points (a) and (b) of Article 4(1) of Regulation (EU) 2018/858;». A clean light vehicle is one with tail-pipe limits and «real driving pollutant emissions below a percentage of the applicable emission limits as laid down in Table 2 of the Annex; or». For heavier vehicles the test is the fuel: «using alternative fuels as defined in points (1) and (2) of Article 2 of Directive 2014/94/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council». The definition excludes blends: «In the case of vehicles using liquid biofuels, synthetic and paraffinic fuels, those fuels shall not be blended with conventional fossil fuels;»

The second question is which contracts count, and when: «This Directive shall only apply to such contracts for which the call for competition has been sent after 2 August 2021 or, in cases where a call for competition is not foreseen, where the contracting authority or contracting entity has commenced the procurement procedure after that date.» The recitals add: «Existing contracts should not be retrospectively affected by this Directive.»

*Analytical inference:* a contract whose call for competition was sent before the stated date is outside the Directive, and a contract after it is inside only if it is one of the listed contract types. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular public contract, and the vehicles used on it, fall inside these definitions.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Targets. The core duty falls on States: «Member States shall ensure that the procurement of vehicles and services referred to in Article 3 complies with the minimum procurement targets for clean light-duty vehicles set out in Table 3 of the Annex and for clean heavy-duty vehicles set out in Table 4 of the Annex.» The period structure: «Those targets are expressed as minimum percentages of clean vehicles in the total number of road transport vehicles covered by the aggregate of all contracts referred to in Article 3, awarded between 2 August 2021 and 31 December 2025, for the first reference period, and between 1 January 2026 and 31 December 2030, for the second reference period.» The recitals call these «two reference periods ending in 2025 and in 2030». The Annex sets the percentages per Member State: «Table 3: Minimum procurement targets for the share of clean light-duty vehicles in accordance with Table 2 in the total number of light-duty vehicles covered by contracts referred to in Article 3 at Member State level» and «Table 4: Minimum procurement targets for the share of clean heavy-duty vehicles in the total number of heavy-duty vehicles covered by contracts referred to in Article 3 at Member State level». For buses: «Half of the minimum target for the share of clean buses has to be fulfilled by procuring zero-emission buses as defined in point 5 of Article 4.»

Counting. «For the purpose of calculating the minimum procurement targets, the date of the public procurement to be taken into account is the date of completion of the public procurement procedure, by way of awarding of the contract.» For vehicle contracts: «In the case of contracts referred to in point (a) of Article 3(1), the number of road transport vehicles purchased, leased, rented or hire-purchased under each contract shall be taken into account for the purpose of assessing compliance with the minimum procurement targets.» For service contracts: «In the case of contracts referred to in points (b) and (c) of Article 3(1), the number of road transport vehicles to be used for the provision of the services covered by each contract shall be taken into account for the purpose of assessing compliance with the minimum procurement targets.» Retrofits count: «Vehicles that meet the definition of clean vehicle under point 4 of Article 4 or of zero-emission heavy-duty vehicle under point 5 of Article 4 as a result of retrofitting may be counted as clean vehicles or zero-emission heavy-duty vehicles, respectively, for the purpose of compliance with the minimum procurement targets.»

After the second period. «Where new targets for the period after 1 January 2030 are not adopted, the targets set for the second reference period shall continue to apply, and shall be calculated in accordance with paragraphs 1 to 5, over subsequent five-year periods.» States may go further: «Member States may apply or authorise their contracting authorities or contracting entities to apply higher national targets or more stringent requirements than those referred to in the Annex.»

Scope and exemptions. The services in scope are limited by a test of the vehicles: «The services covered by the scope of this Directive, such as public road transport services, special purpose road transport passenger services, non-scheduled passenger transport, as well as specific mail and parcel services and refuse collection services, should be those where the vehicles that are used for the provision of these services fall within the vehicle categories covered by this Directive, and where they represent a major element in the contract.» States may exempt some vehicles: «Member States may exempt from the requirements laid down in this Directive vehicles referred to in point (d) of Article 2(2) and in points (a) and (b) of Article 2(3) of Regulation (EU) 2018/858 of the European Parliament and of the Council».

Penalty summary. The Directive states no penalty, fine or sanction for a supplier or a buyer. Implementation is left to national law: the transposition article asks States to bring into force their own laws.

*Analytical inference:* every duty above falls on a Member State, and the counting rules show that a service contract's vehicles feed the State's percentage. The quoted text states no price effect, surcharge or cost for a supplier, so how a buyer's compliance cost reaches a supplier's quote is a gap. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether national transposing law or a tender condition gives any of these target duties a consequence for a business that supplies vehicles or road transport services to a public buyer.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Directive sets procurement targets for public buyers, not rules for products a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Member States report to the Commission in steps. The first report is a short one: «By 2 August 2022 Member States shall inform the Commission of the measures taken to implement this Directive and of the Member States' intentions regarding future implementation activities, including the timing and possible effort-sharing between different levels of governance, as well as on any other information which the Member State considers relevant.» The regular report follows: «By 18 April 2026, and every three years thereafter, Member States shall submit to the Commission a report on the implementation of this Directive.» Both dates have passed. The recitals describe the same cycle: «a first comprehensive report on the implementation of the minimum procurement targets in 2026 and every three years thereafter». The reports carry vehicle counts: «Those reports shall also include the number and the categories of vehicles covered by the contracts referred to in Article 3(1) of this Directive, based on the data provided by the Commission in accordance with paragraph 3 of this Article.» The Commission helps States with the data: «In order to assist the Member States in their reporting obligations, the Commission shall collate and publish the number and the categories of vehicles covered by the contracts referred to in points (a) and (c) of Article 3(1) of this Directive by extracting the relevant data from contract award notices published on the Tenders Electronic Daily (TED) database in accordance with Directives 2014/24/EU and 2014/25/EU.» States also pass on their laws: «Member States shall communicate to the Commission the text of the main measures of national law which they adopt in the field covered by this Directive.»

*Analytical inference:* all registration and reporting duties here run between Member States and the Commission. The text states no registration or report by a freight business. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether national law adds a report or registration for suppliers to public buyers.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Directive builds no system for a supplier, but the counting of vehicles by category makes a fleet record the thing a public buyer may ask about.

- A contracts administrator keeps, for each public road transport contract, a fleet list that gives every vehicle's category (M or N as the Directive defines it) and its fuel type, so the answer is ready when a buyer asks what vehicles will be used.
- A fleet planner flags each vehicle on that list that runs on liquid biofuel, synthetic or paraffinic fuel, each time the fleet list is updated for a new bid or a contract renewal, because the Directive's definition allows such fuels only when they are not blended with conventional fossil fuels.

*Analytical inference:* these steps rest on the Directive's vehicle categories, its fuel definition and the buyer's reporting need described in Section 10. The Directive does not itself ask a supplier for this record. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a buyer may require such a record from a supplier under the tender terms and national law.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

The Directive's own exemption is a State option and is quoted in Section 8. The recitals exclude work vehicles: «The requirements provided for in this Directive should not apply to vehicles that are designed and constructed specifically to perform works and which are not suitable for carrying passengers or for transporting goods.»

*Analytical inference:* the work-vehicle exclusion is worded around vehicles not suitable for carrying passengers or transporting goods, and the text states nothing that excludes a goods vehicle by it. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific vehicle falls under a State's exemption.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope

This document covers «COMMISSION IMPLEMENTING REGULATION (EU) 2024/994 of 2 April 2024 laying down operational details of the product database established under Regulation (EU) 2017/1369 of the European Parliament and of the Council (Text with EEA relevance)». Its jurisdiction is the European Union: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» What the Regulation sets is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

*Analytical inference:* the Regulation is operational detail for a database set up by Regulation (EU) 2017/1369, so it is read with that text for the duties it serves, which the captured text does not reproduce.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Commission runs a product database for energy labels: «the Commission put in place the European Product Registry for Energy Labelling (EPREL) system to establish a product database. The EPREL system consists of two parts: a public system providing free access to public information on product models placed on the Union market, and a compliance system where suppliers provide both the public and the technical information on those product models, and that can be accessed by Member State market surveillance authorities.» The Regulation's subject: «Article 1 Subject matter and scope 1. This Regulation sets out operational details for the functioning of the product database established in line with Article 12 of Regulation (EU) 2017/1369 and detailed rules applying to suppliers placing on the Union market: (a) energy-related products covered by delegated acts supplementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1369 and Directive 2010/30/EU; (b) tyres covered by Regulation (EU) 2020/740 or by delegated acts supplementing it.»

*Analytical inference:* the products in scope are labelled energy-related products and labelled tyres. A freight business meets the Regulation through clients that supply those products, because a supplier registers product models before placing units on the market: «Suppliers should carry out the electronic verification process with a view to providing evidence of their identity and establishment in the Union in order to register the relevant models before placing any unit of those product models on the Union market.» The text states no cost for a freight business.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no reader deadline falls in the next month. The one forward date is a renewal deadline for suppliers, not for a freight business: «By 22 April 2027, suppliers that have been verified with an electronic seal according to the format set under paragraph 1 shall renew their verification by providing a qualified electronic seal as set out in Article 4.»

- A client-relations lead, at the next account review and before 22 April 2027: asks each client that supplies labelled energy-related products or labelled tyres whether its EPREL verification used the transitional seal format and who renews it.
- A client-relations lead, at the same review: notes in the client file which clients register their own models in EPREL, because only a verified supplier may do so.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the renewal date above and on the verification requirement in section 8; the text states no cost and no fine. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any client of the business is an EPREL supplier in the sense of the Regulation.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names the supplier, the dealer or distributor, the Member State market surveillance authority and the Commission. The supplier definition: «‘EPREL supplier’ means a natural person or legal person in its capacity to act as a supplier for registering product models in the product database» Dealers and distributors: «suppliers shall communicate the EPREL model registration number to dealers or to distributors, as applicable. 2. To allow for the consultation of a model’s registration in EPREL, the dealer or the distributor shall ensure that the QR code is readable when putting a product model or tyre in display for sale.» A forwarder is not named.

*Analytical inference:* a freight business sits outside the named chain unless it is itself a supplier, dealer or distributor of labelled products. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business that imports or stocks labelled products for a client counts as a supplier or distributor.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Who counts as a supplier decides whether the verification rule applies. For natural persons the recitals say: «Natural persons should be considered suppliers in EPREL only if they provide evidence of the exercise of an economic activity compatible with placing products on the Union market and if they prove their establishment in the Union.»

*Analytical inference:* a legal person or a natural person is a supplier only in its capacity to register product models; being a carrier of the products is not stated to make it one. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the capacity in which a freight business handles a labelled product.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Scope. «Article 1 Subject matter and scope 1. This Regulation sets out operational details for the functioning of the product database established in line with Article 12 of Regulation (EU) 2017/1369 and detailed rules applying to suppliers placing on the Union market: (a) energy-related products covered by delegated acts supplementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1369 and Directive 2010/30/EU; (b) tyres covered by Regulation (EU) 2020/740 or by delegated acts supplementing it.»

Verification. «Suppliers of products specified in Article 1(1) points (a) and (b) shall be verified suppliers. 2. Only verified suppliers may register product models in EPREL and perform any modification relating to existing ones.» Legal persons: «Suppliers that are legal persons shall submit evidence of their identity and of their establishment within the Union by means of a qualified electronic seal supported by a qualified certificate for electronic seal, issued by a qualified trust service provider pursuant to Regulation (EU) No 910/2014.» Natural persons: «Suppliers that are natural persons shall submit evidence of their identity by means of a qualified electronic signature.»

Consequence of not being verified. «Models registered in EPREL by entities not verified shall not be listed in the search results in public EPREL website. When such a model is retrieved from EPREL by scanning a QR code or by any other means a text shall indicate that the model was registered by an unverified supplier.»

Registration. «The registration by a supplier of a product model in EPREL shall be deemed completed only after all the following parameter values have been entered and the relevant documents have been uploaded in EPREL for each model: (a) all values related to the parameters and documents required under Regulation (EU) 2017/1369, Regulation (EU) 2020/740 or any delegated act adopted under those regulations applicable to the product; (b) the date of placing on the market of the first unit of the particular model.»

Dealers and distributors. «suppliers shall communicate the EPREL model registration number to dealers or to distributors, as applicable. 2. To allow for the consultation of a model’s registration in EPREL, the dealer or the distributor shall ensure that the QR code is readable when putting a product model or tyre in display for sale.»

Commission data access. «The Commission shall make the public parameter values, label and product information sheet of registered models available by the means of Application Programming Interfaces (API), subject to acceptance of terms of use.»

Penalty. No penalty or sanction provision is among the pages held; the only consequences stated are the public listing consequence above and the loss of verified status.

*Analytical inference:* the cause is the verification requirement; the mechanical consequence is that only a verified supplier can register or change a model, and an unverified supplier's models drop out of public search; the effect for a freight business is limited to clients that supply labelled products. The text does not state how any cost reaches a rate. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which clients are suppliers, and whether national law adds a penalty.

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 2; extracted as FACT: 8.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The Regulation is itself the registration scheme. Suppliers register models in the database: «Suppliers shall register product models either by using the interactive EPREL compliance website or by uploading the model data using the latest version of the data exchange model available.» A completed registration needs: «The registration by a supplier of a product model in EPREL shall be deemed completed only after all the following parameter values have been entered and the relevant documents have been uploaded in EPREL for each model: (a) all values related to the parameters and documents required under Regulation (EU) 2017/1369, Regulation (EU) 2020/740 or any delegated act adopted under those regulations applicable to the product; (b) the date of placing on the market of the first unit of the particular model.» The end date of a model is entered: «The date of end of placing on the market of each product model may be entered as a future date or shall be entered in EPREL within 90 days after its occurrence» Contact points: «Suppliers shall also identify in the compliance part of EPREL, as their compliance contact point, the contact details of the department or sector that ensures cooperation with market surveillance authorities, including a telephone number, a physical address within the EU and a generic email address not containing personal data.»

*Analytical inference:* each of these duties falls on the supplier; a freight business with no supplier role has no registration step under the text. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business holds a supplier role, which would bring these registration duties to it.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the system work in the text falls on suppliers. Access rights: «Each supplier shall be responsible for the management of the access rights to their own data by members of its own EPREL supplier organisation. At least one user shall be appointed as being responsible for the supplier and for managing other user profiles and their access rights.» Inactive suppliers: «A previously verified supplier shall lose status of ‘verified’ if it appears to be inactive based on activity logs for over one year and is not responsive after a double email alert. Article 7 applies in such a case.»

- A client-relations lead, at each client onboarding or annual review: asks a client that is a supplier who its named responsible user is and whether the account is active, because inactivity for over one year costs the verified status.

*Operational implication:* the text puts these duties on the supplier, not on a freight business. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business holds a supplier role at all.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

A transitional measure allowed a different seal format for a time: «In derogation to points (a) and (d) of Article 4(3) and until 22 April 2025, suppliers that are legal persons may submit a qualified electronic seal where the three-character legal person identity type reference may be set to one of the following values:»

*Analytical inference:* that allowance has ended, and the renewal duty in section 3 is its other end. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given supplier used the transitional format.

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 2 April 2024: adopted. «Done at Brussels, 2 April 2024.»
- 22 October 2024: Articles 3, 4, 5, 7, 11 and 15 apply (date passed). «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . It shall apply from the same day. Articles 3, 4, 5, 7, 11 and 15 shall apply from 22 October 2024.»
- 22 April 2025: the transitional seal format ends (date passed). «In derogation to points (a) and (d) of Article 4(3) and until 22 April 2025, suppliers that are legal persons may submit a qualified electronic seal where the three-character legal person identity type reference may be set to one of the following values:»
- 22 April 2027: suppliers verified under the transitional format renew their verification. «By 22 April 2027, suppliers that have been verified with an electronic seal according to the format set under paragraph 1 shall renew their verification by providing a qualified electronic seal as set out in Article 4.»

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2024/1610 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 14 May 2024 amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1242 as regards strengthening the CO 2 emission performance standards for new heavy-duty vehicles and integrating reporting obligations, amending Regulation (EU) 2018/858 and repealing Regulation (EU) 2018/956», the Union's 2024 revision of its CO2 standards for lorries, buses, coaches and trailers. It changes an earlier regulation; the targets it sets sit on manufacturers. The Parliament's procedure page gives its purpose: «PURPOSE: to approve stricter CO2 emission standards for heavy duty vehicles.» What the Regulation requires is stated from its own words; what it means for the workspace is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

Its reach: «heavy-duty vehicles shall be considered as new heavy-duty vehicles in a given reporting period, if they are registered in the Union for the first time in that reporting period and have not been previously registered outside the Union.»

It enters into force as its final article states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union» and «It shall apply from 1 July 2024.»

*Analytical inference:* the scope is vehicles first registered in the Union, so a lorry, bus, coach or trailer first registered in a Member State falls under the manufacturer's target for that period; it rests on the registration sentence quoted above.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

What changed. «The original CO 2 standards required the emissions from most new trucks to be 15% lower by 2025 and 30% lower by 2030 than the 2019 reporting period. The revised standards maintain the CO 2 reduction target of 15% for 2025 and raise the 2030 target to 45% while introducing a 65% reduction target for 2035 and a 90% target for 2040.» The revision widens what is covered: «Heavy-duty vehicles that made up 92% of sales in 2023 are now covered under the new regulation.» and «Following this revision, Regulation (EU) 2019/1242 covers nearly all HDV emissions as it applies not only to heavy lorries but also to medium lorries, city buses, coaches, and trailers.» The reason: «In 2021, they were responsible for 28% of CO 2 emissions from the European road transport sector.» and «The European Climate Law requires the EU to achieve climate neutrality by 2050.»

Why it applies to the workspace: the workspace buys, leases or subcontracts road transport with heavy-duty vehicles, so the vehicles on offer, and the share that are zero-emission, are shaped by the manufacturers' targets.

*Analytical inference:* the targets bind manufacturers, not operators, so the workspace meets them through vehicle supply and the infrastructure that follows; it rests on the manufacturer sentence in section 1 and the purpose statement above. The capture states no price effect on vehicles or on road transport rates.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: the limits are on manufacturers, the next step-down is 2030, and the Commission has a report due in 2027 on large fleet operators. «By 30 June 2027, the Commission shall submit to the European Parliament and to the Council a report which contains an analysis of the potential need for and impact of initiatives to increase the share of zero-emission heavy-duty motor vehicles owned or leased by large fleet operators.»

- Fleet purchasing lead, at the next purchase or lease of a heavy lorry, bus, coach or trailer: ask the supplier which vehicle sub-group the model belongs to and whether a zero-emission version is offered, and record the answer in the vehicle file.
- Fleet purchasing lead, before each such decision: read the public record of reported vehicle data: «The central register shall be publicly available» for CO2 and fuel consumption values.
- Fleet manager, before 30 June 2027: record whether the workspace owns or leases heavy-duty motor vehicles in a number that could be called a large fleet, because of the 2027 report above.
- Fleet purchasing lead, before ordering vehicles for delivery after 1 July 2026: ask each supplier how the pending December 2025 proposal to ease the 2030 target, described in section 6, affects the zero-emission models offered.

*Analytical inference:* each step rests on the quoted sentences; the capture holds no definition of a large fleet operator and states no consequence for an operator from the report. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace's own or leased vehicles would be treated as those of a large fleet operator, and what the pending proposal changes for vehicle supply.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The roles. The manufacturer: «“manufacturer” means the person or body to which the vehicles registered in a given period have been attributed in accordance with Article 7a;» The reporter: «“reporter” means an entity which is responsible for the reporting of data to the Commission;» The Member States report registrations: «the competent authorities of the Member States shall report those data for the previous reporting period of 1 July to 30 June to the Commission». The record: «The European Environment Agency shall manage the central register on behalf of the Commission.» Public buyers of urban buses: «Contracting authorities and contracting entities shall base the award of public supply contracts for the purchase, lease, rent or hire-purchase of new zero-emission urban buses, as well as of public service contracts having as their main subject matter the use of such urban buses, on the most economically advantageous tender which shall include the best price-quality ratio.»

A forwarder is not named in the text held here, and neither is any operator of the vehicles as a duty holder.

*Analytical inference:* the workspace is not in the compliance chain as a duty holder; it sits downstream as a buyer, lessee or user of the vehicles, and as a contracting party for urban buses only if it is a public contracting authority, which the capture does not suggest. It rests on the role definitions quoted above. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any operator duty arises from a lease or ownership arrangement, since the quoted definitions attach to manufacturers and reporters.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

Dated steps and open reviews at the date of this document.

- A proposal to ease the 2030 target: «The proposed targeted amendment allows manufacturers to collect more emission credits in the years before 2030 than in the current Regulation.»
- A report on retrofitted vehicles was due: «By 30 June 2025, the Commission shall submit to the European Parliament and to the Council a report which considers the need to facilitate the uptake on the Union market of heavy-duty vehicles which are retrofitted to become zero-emission heavy-duty vehicles». The date has passed; the capture does not say the report was submitted.
- A report on renewable fuels was due: «the Commission shall by 31 December 2025 present a report to the European Parliament and to the Council with a comprehensive analysis of the need to further incentivise the uptake of advanced biofuels and biogas and renewable fuels of non-biological origin in the heavy-duty vehicles sector». The date has passed; the capture does not say the report was presented.
- The report on large fleet operators is due by 30 June 2027, as quoted in section 3.
- The review of the Regulation: «By 31 December 2027, the Commission shall review the effectiveness and impact of this Regulation», assessing among other points «the level of the excess CO 2 emissions premium, to ensure that it exceeds the average marginal costs of the technologies needed to meet the CO 2 emissions reduction targets».

*Analytical inference:* the review of the premium level and the pending proposal are the two items that can move a manufacturer's cost of missing a target, and with it the supply of lower-emission vehicles; the capture states no date for the proposal's adoption. They rest on the review and proposal sentences quoted above.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

**Targets.** «The average CO 2 emissions of the Union fleet of new heavy-duty motor vehicles, other than special purpose vehicles, off-road vehicles and off-road special purpose vehicles shall be reduced by the following percentages compared to the average CO 2 emissions of the reporting period of the year 2019: (a) 15 % for vehicle sub-groups 4-UD, 4-RD, 4-LH, 5-RD, 5-LH, 9-RD, 9-LH, 10-RD and 10-LH for the reporting periods of the years 2025 to 2029; (b) 45 % for all vehicle sub-groups other than vocational vehicles for the reporting periods of the years 2030 to 2034; (c) 65 % for all vehicle sub-groups for the reporting periods of the years 2035 to 2039; (d) 90 % for all vehicle sub-groups for the reporting periods of the year 2040 onwards.»

**Trailers and reference periods.** «starting in 2030, CO 2 emissions must be reduced by 10% for new semi-trailers and by 7,5% for new trailers other than semi-trailers.» The Annex I table of the Regulation lists, for trailers, a zero and then three values: «Trailers 111, 111V, 112, 112V, 113, 121, 121V, 122, 122V, 123, 123V, 124, 124V, 125, 126, 131, 131V, 132, 132V, 133 0 7,5 % 7,5 % 7,5 %» and for semi-trailers «Semi-trailers For reporting periods of the years before 2025, all CO 2 emissions reduction targets rf sg and rfp sg shall be 0. 421, 421v, 422, 422v, 423, 431, 431v, 432, 432v, 433, 611, 612, 611V, 612V, 621, 623, 621V, 622, 622V, 623V, 624, 624V, 625, 631, 631v, 632, 632v, 633 0 10 % 10 % 10 %». The Commission page gives the reference periods: «2019 for vehicles regulated under previous standards» and «2025 for coaches, trailers, and medium lorries». The Parliament's summary, a secondary statement that conflicts with the Annex table and the Commission page on the start, says: «Emissions reduction targets are also set for trailers (7.5%) and semi-trailers (10%), starting from 2040.»

**Urban buses.** «For heavy-duty vehicles referred to in the fourth column of the table in point 4.2 of Annex I (“urban buses”), manufacturers shall comply with the 90 % and 100 % minimum shares of zero-emission heavy-duty vehicles in their fleet of new heavy-duty vehicles in accordance with point 4.3.2 of Annex I.» «The new rules introduce a 100% zero-emission target for new urban buses by 2035 , with an intermediate target of 90% for this category by 2030.»

**Premium.** «Where a manufacturer is found, pursuant to paragraph 2, to have excess CO 2 emissions in a given reporting period from 2025 onwards, the Commission shall impose an excess CO 2 emissions premium, calculated in accordance with the following formula: (excess CO 2 emissions premium) = (excess CO 2 emissions × 4 250 EUR/gCO 2 /tkm).»

**Reporting.** «By 30 September of each year, they shall report those data to the Commission for each new heavy-duty vehicle» «The Commission may impose an administrative fine in each of the following cases: (a) where it finds that the data reported by the manufacturer pursuant to Article 13b of this Regulation deviate from the data resulting from the manufacturer’s records file or the engine type-approval certificate issued within the framework of Regulation (EC) No 595/2009, and the deviation is intentional or due to serious negligence; (b) where the data are not submitted within the deadline referred to in Article 13b(1), second subparagraph, and the delay cannot be duly justified.»

**Scope of the reporting rules after the revision.** «Regulation (EU) 2019/1242 should be amended in order to cover the same scope as Regulation (EU) 2018/956»

**Vehicles outside the target.** «This paragraph shall not apply to heavy-duty vehicles that are exempted pursuant to Article 6b.»

**Transition.** «Notwithstanding Article 3, in respect of reporting periods prior to 1 July 2024, Regulation (EU) 2019/1242 as applicable on 30 June 2024 and Regulation (EU) 2018/956 as applicable on 30 June 2024 shall continue to apply.» «Regulation (EU) 2018/956 is repealed with effect from 1 July 2024.»

*Analytical inference:* every obligation above falls on manufacturers, reporters or the Commission; none is placed on an operator of the vehicles, and the capture states no pass-through of the premium to vehicle prices. It rests on the quoted target, premium and reporting sentences. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any contract that moves a manufacturer's cost to a buyer is valid, and which vehicle sub-group a given model belongs to for the target that applies.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Member States report registrations: «By 30 September of each year, starting in 2020, the competent authorities of the Member States shall report those data for the previous reporting period of 1 July to 30 June to the Commission». Manufacturers report vehicle data: «Manufacturers or other entities that are responsible for the determination of the CO 2 emissions of a heavy-duty vehicle and are subject to Article 9 of Regulation (EU) 2017/2400 or Article 8 of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/1362 shall report the data for new heavy-duty vehicles in accordance with Part B of Annex IV to this Regulation.» The data go to a public record: «The Commission shall keep a central register for the data on heavy-duty vehicles (“the central register”) reported pursuant to Articles 13a and 13b.» The Parliament's summary agrees: «The central register will be publicly available.»

*Analytical inference:* the registration and reporting duties sit with Member State authorities and manufacturers; the text states none on a vehicle operator, and the public register is the part a buyer can read. It rests on the reporting sentences quoted above. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any reporting duty reaches an operator that owns or leases vehicles, since the quoted sentences attach to manufacturers and Member State authorities.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Regulation builds no system for an operator; the work is the workspace's own use of what is published. The record is described as: «The central register shall be publicly available with the exception of data entries listed in point 3.2 of Annex V.»

- Fleet purchasing lead, at the next vehicle purchase or lease: add to the vehicle purchase and lease file a field for the vehicle sub-group, the reported CO2 and fuel consumption values from the public register, and whether the model is zero-emission, so that quotes can be compared on those values.
- Bid manager, at the next urban bus service tender: add a line asking the contracting authority which award criteria it uses: «Contracting authorities and contracting entities shall use at least two of the following criteria as technical specifications or as award criteria, at least one of which shall relate to the tender’s contribution to the security of supply»
- Fleet purchasing lead, before the 2030 step-down: close the gap that the vehicle file holds price and payload but no CO2 value, by adding the field so that comparisons across suppliers are possible.

*Analytical inference:* the steps rest on the public register and the urban bus procurement sentences quoted above; the Regulation does not require the workspace to keep any record. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a tender for bus services falls within the contracting-authority rule quoted above.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Manufacturers producing few vehicles: «If a manufacturer registers fewer than 100 new heavy-duty vehicles in a given reporting period, the average specific CO 2 emissions as provided for in Article 4 and in point 2.7 of Annex I and the specific CO 2 emissions targets as provided for in Article 6 and in point 4.1 of Annex I shall be set at “0” for that reporting period.» Vehicles registered only to be moved out of the Union: «This Regulation shall not apply to heavy-duty vehicles that are registered for the first time for a period not exceeding one month and that are registered for the sole purpose of transfer to a country outside the Union.» Services: «Heavy-duty vehicles registered for use by civil protection services, fire services, forces responsible for maintaining public order or urgent medical care services shall be subject to this Article, irrespective of whether they are exempted from Article 3a.» Inter-urban buses: «Inter-urban buses will be exempt from this target, as they will be regarded as coaches for the purposes of measuring emissions reduction.»

*Analytical inference:* the small-manufacturer rule and the transfer rule sit on the manufacturer's side; a buyer of a vehicle from a small manufacturer meets no target through it, and inter-urban buses count as coaches. It rests on the quoted exemption sentences. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific vehicle falls under the exemption for few vehicles or is an urban or inter-urban bus.

## 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

Research and analysis from the International Council on Clean Transportation, labelled as such: «This policy update summarizes the main elements of the revised EU CO 2 standards for trucks and buses, Europe’s cornerstone regulation to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from the heavy-duty vehicle sector.» It adds: «Trucks and buses comprise 2% of the vehicles on the road in Europe but are the second largest contributors to CO2 emissions in transport.»

*Analytical inference:* the research body frames the Regulation as the main measure on heavy-vehicle CO2 in the Union; it rests on the quoted summary sentence and is not a regulator statement.
