   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2026/667 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 11 March 2026 amending Regulation (EU) 2021/1119 as regards the setting of a Union intermediate climate target for 2040». Its jurisdiction is the European Union: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» What the Regulation sets is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

*Analytical inference:* the Regulation amends the European Climate Law, Regulation (EU) 2021/1119, so the earlier text is read with it; the captured text does not reproduce that law.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation adds a 2040 step to the Union's climate law. The law already holds the long-term objective: «the Union has enshrined in legislation a binding objective of economy-wide climate neutrality by 2050» and an earlier step: «That Regulation also established a binding intermediate Union climate target for 2030» The new amendment: «This Regulation also sets out a binding Union target for 2040.» The target itself: «In order to reach the climate-neutrality objective set out in Article 2(1), the binding Union 2040 climate target shall be a reduction of net greenhouse gas emissions (emissions after deduction of removals) by 90 % compared to 1990 levels by 2040.» Entry into force: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union»

It also postpones carbon pricing on road fuel: «The operation of emissions trading for buildings, road transport and additional sectors set out in Chapter IVa of Directive 2003/87/EC shall be postponed until 2028.» The recital that explains it: «In order to ensure a smooth transition to the emissions trading system for buildings, road transport and additional sectors set out in Chapter IVa of Directive 2003/87/EC (the ‘ETS2’), the operation of emissions trading for those sectors should be postponed by one year»

The recitals name the shipping and aviation industries among others, and the wider setting: «particular attention should be paid to traditional industries, notably the automotive, shipping and aviation industries» «to organise a strategic dialogue on the post-2030 framework with all relevant sectors, including industry and transport» «a global level playing field including through the effective implementation and extension of the carbon border adjustment mechanism ( 7 ) to downstream goods»

*Analytical inference:* a freight business is not given a duty by this text. The target and the postponement change the timetable of the carbon rules that later laws will apply, so any effect on rates and contracts comes through other instruments the captured text does not hold. The text states no cost figure.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no reader deadline falls in the next month and the text puts no duty on a freight business. The next dated step is the Commission's first assessment: «From 6 March 2027 and every two years thereafter, the Commission shall assess and report on the implementation of the intermediate targets and decarbonisation trajectories set out in this Regulation, taking into account the latest scientific evidence, technological advances and evolving challenges to and opportunities for the Union’s global competitiveness.»

- A pricing lead, at the next road transport contract renewal: checks each fuel surcharge clause that cites a start date for emissions trading on road fuel, and aligns it with the postponement until 2028 quoted in section 2.
- A regulatory-affairs lead, before 6 March 2027: logs that date as the first Commission assessment under the new Article 4(8) and, when it is published, reads it for proposals on transport fuels.

*Operational implication:* both steps use only dates the text states. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given contract clause is tied to the earlier start date for emissions trading on road transport.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names the Commission, the Member States and the Union as actors. «With a view to the period after 2030, the Commission shall review relevant Union legislation in order to enable the achievement of the target set out in paragraph 3 of this Article and the climate-neutrality objective set out in Article 2(1) and consider taking the necessary measures as appropriate» No supply chain role such as a carrier, shipper or forwarder is named.

*Analytical inference:* a freight business stands downstream of this text, as a customer or contract party of the operators that later laws will bind. *Legal Confirmation Required:* none of the text's duties reaches a freight business directly; counsel confirms this against the earlier Regulation (EU) 2021/1119.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Commission has several things to do next. Legislation review: «With a view to the period after 2030, the Commission shall review relevant Union legislation in order to enable the achievement of the target set out in paragraph 3 of this Article and the climate-neutrality objective set out in Article 2(1) and consider taking the necessary measures as appropriate» Emissions trading review: «the review of Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 8 ) in 2026» Free allocation: «The Commission should consider in a timely manner a slower phase-out pathway for free allocation of allowances from 2028 onwards to support decarbonisation, investment and employment in the Union, including through an industrial decarbonisation bank and a review of the market stability reserve ( 11 ) , while minimising the risk of carbon leakage.» The trajectory: «The current EU ETS trajectory should be revised in the upcoming review of Directive 2003/87/EC to take into account the agreed 2040 target in a manner that would allow for a limited amount of emissions after 2039.» Reports and proposals: «The Commission’s report shall be accompanied, where appropriate, by legislative proposals to revise this Regulation, including the intermediate 2040 target»

*Analytical inference:* these are the points where the 2040 target turns into rules that can reach freight, but the text gives no date for the proposals; the 2026 review is the only dated step besides the 6 March 2027 assessment. Sections 8 and 14 list the dates.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

The target. «In order to reach the climate-neutrality objective set out in Article 2(1), the binding Union 2040 climate target shall be a reduction of net greenhouse gas emissions (emissions after deduction of removals) by 90 % compared to 1990 levels by 2040.»

Review after 2030. «With a view to the period after 2030, the Commission shall review relevant Union legislation in order to enable the achievement of the target set out in paragraph 3 of this Article and the climate-neutrality objective set out in Article 2(1) and consider taking the necessary measures as appropriate»

International credits. «from 2036, an adequate contribution towards the 2040 climate target of high-quality international credits under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement of up to 5 % of 1990 Union net emissions, corresponding to a domestic reduction of net greenhouse gas emissions by 85 % compared to 1990 levels by 2040» «a pilot period from 2031 to 2035 to initiate a high-quality and high-integrity international credit market may be considered» «the origin, quality criteria and other conditions concerning the acquisition and use of any such credits shall be regulated in Union law»

Removals. «(b) the role of domestic permanent removals under the system established by Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council ( *1 ) for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading within the Union (the “EU ETS”) to compensate for residual hard-to-abate emissions»

Fuels for transport. «(p) the role of zero-, low carbon and renewable fuels in the decarbonisation of transport, including road transport beyond 2030 and concrete measures to assist manufacturers of heavy-duty vehicles to reach their targets, taking into account European content»

Reporting. «From 6 March 2027 and every two years thereafter, the Commission shall assess and report on the implementation of the intermediate targets and decarbonisation trajectories set out in this Regulation, taking into account the latest scientific evidence, technological advances and evolving challenges to and opportunities for the Union’s global competitiveness.»

Emissions trading for road transport and buildings. «The operation of emissions trading for buildings, road transport and additional sectors set out in Chapter IVa of Directive 2003/87/EC shall be postponed until 2028.»

Penalty. The captured text states no penalty, fine or sanction.

*Analytical inference:* the cause is a Union target; the mechanical consequence is that the Commission must reflect the listed elements in its post-2030 proposals, including low carbon fuels for road transport; the effect for freight arrives through later laws. The text does not state how any cost reaches a rate. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which later instruments will carry the 2040 target into transport rules, and whether the postponement alters any contract term.

No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 to 3 beyond the dates quoted above. No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 3. No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 3 beyond the sectors named in Article 2.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The captured text states no registration duty; the only report it sets is the Commission's. The report: «From 6 March 2027 and every two years thereafter, the Commission shall assess and report on the implementation of the intermediate targets and decarbonisation trajectories set out in this Regulation, taking into account the latest scientific evidence, technological advances and evolving challenges to and opportunities for the Union’s global competitiveness.»

*Analytical inference:* the report is the Commission's, so a freight business has no filing; it is a source of dated signals for transport fuels and the carbon rules.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: nothing in the text sets a system to build for a freight business.

- A pricing lead, at each road transport quote that carries a fuel surcharge: records the date of the clause that cites emissions trading, so it can be updated against the postponement until 2028.

*Operational implication:* the record is the business's own; the text sets no system.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

The Commission may adjust the target if natural removals fall short: «if the Commission finds that the estimated level of net natural removals for 2040 is significantly diverging from what would be required to achieve the 2040 intermediate target, including where that divergence is due to natural disturbances, the Commission shall propose, where appropriate, measures at Union level, including, if necessary, an adjustment of the 2040 intermediate target corresponding to, and within the limits of, the possible shortfalls»

*Analytical inference:* the 2040 target is not fixed for all cases; the shortfall route is a limited adjustment, within the limits the text names. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the conditions under which the adjustment could be proposed.

- 11 March 2026: adopted. «Done at Strasbourg, 11 March 2026.»
- 18 March 2026: published in the Official Journal. «L series 2026/667 18.3.2026»
- 6 March 2027: first Commission assessment, then every two years. «From 6 March 2027 and every two years thereafter, the Commission shall assess and report on the implementation of the intermediate targets and decarbonisation trajectories set out in this Regulation, taking into account the latest scientific evidence, technological advances and evolving challenges to and opportunities for the Union’s global competitiveness.»
- 2028: emissions trading for buildings, road transport and additional sectors postponed until this year. «The operation of emissions trading for buildings, road transport and additional sectors set out in Chapter IVa of Directive 2003/87/EC shall be postponed until 2028.»
- 2036: the Commission is to ensure its proposals reflect international credits of up to 5 % of 1990 Union net emissions from this year. «from 2036, an adequate contribution towards the 2040 climate target of high-quality international credits under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement of up to 5 % of 1990 Union net emissions, corresponding to a domestic reduction of net greenhouse gas emissions by 85 % compared to 1990 levels by 2040»
- 2040: binding 90 % net reduction target. «In order to reach the climate-neutrality objective set out in Article 2(1), the binding Union 2040 climate target shall be a reduction of net greenhouse gas emissions (emissions after deduction of removals) by 90 % compared to 1990 levels by 2040.»

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2019/1242 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 20 June 2019 setting CO 2 emission performance standards for new heavy-duty vehicles», as revised by «06/06/2024 Regulation (EU) 2024/1610 amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1242 on strengthening CO 2 emission standards for heavy-duty vehicles». The 2019 text set the first Union CO2 standards for heavy lorries; the 2024 revision widened them. The limits sit on manufacturers: «manufacturers have to comply with targets for fleet-wide average CO 2 emissions starting from 2025. These targets apply to new HDVs registered in the reporting period of a given year, namely from 1 July of that year to 30 June of the following year.» What the Regulation requires is stated from its own words; what it means for the workspace is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

Its reach: «heavy-duty vehicles shall be considered as new heavy-duty vehicles in a given reporting period, if they are registered in the Union for the first time in that reporting period and have not been previously registered outside the Union.»

It enters into force as its final article states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union»

*Analytical inference:* the scope is vehicles first registered in the Union, so a lorry, bus, coach or trailer first registered in a Member State falls under the manufacturer's target for that period; it rests on the registration sentence quoted above.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

«The term 'heavy-duty vehicles' (HDVs) refers to: Lorries» The reason for the Regulation: «HDVs are responsible for more than a quarter of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from road transport in the EU, and for over 6% of total EU GHG emissions.» The revision widened what is covered: «Following this revision, Regulation (EU) 2019/1242 covers nearly all HDV emissions as it applies not only to heavy lorries but also to medium lorries, city buses, coaches, and trailers.» The Commission states what the standards are meant to do for operators: «Reducing the fuel expenditure and total cost of ownership for transport operators and all users» and «Increasing the share of zero and low-emission vehicles in the market, and accelerating the roll-out of recharging and re-fuelling infrastructure».

Why it applies to the workspace: the workspace buys, leases or subcontracts road transport with heavy-duty vehicles, so the vehicles on offer, and the share that are zero-emission, are shaped by the manufacturers' targets below.

*Analytical inference:* the targets bind manufacturers, not operators, so the workspace meets them through the supply of vehicles and the infrastructure that follows; it rests on the manufacturer sentence in section 1 and the Commission's statement of purpose above. The capture states no price effect on vehicles or transport rates.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: the limits are on manufacturers, the next step-down comes in 2030, and a proposal to ease it is pending. The Commission describes the proposal: «In December 2025 , the Commission presented the Automotive Package , which set an ambitious yet pragmatic policy framework to ensure climate neutrality by 2050 and strategic independence while providing more flexibility to manufacturers. The Package proposes a targeted amendment to the existing CO 2 emission standards for HDVs , aiming to provide manufacturers with an additional flexibility to ease the compliance with their applicable 2030 CO 2 emissions targets.»

- Fleet purchasing lead, at the next purchase or lease of a heavy lorry, bus, coach or trailer: ask the supplier which vehicle sub-group the model belongs to and whether a zero-emission version is offered, and record the answer in the vehicle file; the sub-group is the unit the targets in section 8 are set by.
- Fleet purchasing lead, before each such decision: read the public record of reported vehicle data: «The central register shall be publicly available» for CO2 and fuel consumption values.
- Fleet manager, before 30 June 2027: record whether the workspace owns or leases heavy-duty motor vehicles in a number that could be called a large fleet, because «By 30 June 2027, the Commission shall submit to the European Parliament and to the Council a report which contains an analysis of the potential need for and impact of initiatives to increase the share of zero-emission heavy-duty motor vehicles owned or leased by large fleet operators.»

*Analytical inference:* each step rests on the quoted sentences; the capture holds no definition of a large fleet operator and states no consequence for an operator from the report. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace's own or leased vehicles would be treated as those of a large fleet operator, and what the pending proposal changes for vehicle supply.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The roles the Regulation defines. The manufacturer: «“manufacturer” means the person or body to which the vehicles registered in a given period have been attributed in accordance with Article 7a;» The reporter: «“reporter” means an entity which is responsible for the reporting of data to the Commission;» The Member States monitor and report registrations: «the competent authorities of the Member States shall report those data for the previous reporting period of 1 July to 30 June to the Commission». ## 8. Substantive Requirements

**Targets.** «The average CO 2 emissions of the Union fleet of new heavy-duty motor vehicles, other than special purpose vehicles, off-road vehicles and off-road special purpose vehicles shall be reduced by the following percentages compared to the average CO 2 emissions of the reporting period of the year 2019: (a) 15 % for vehicle sub-groups 4-UD, 4-RD, 4-LH, 5-RD, 5-LH, 9-RD, 9-LH, 10-RD and 10-LH for the reporting periods of the years 2025 to 2029; (b) 45 % for all vehicle sub-groups other than vocational vehicles for the reporting periods of the years 2030 to 2034; (c) 65 % for all vehicle sub-groups for the reporting periods of the years 2035 to 2039; (d) 90 % for all vehicle sub-groups for the reporting periods of the year 2040 onwards.» The Commission summarises: «the revised targets are also more ambitious, aiming for increasing CO 2 emission reductions in the coming decades: 45% by 2030 65% by 2035 90% by 2040»

**Reference periods.** «2019 for vehicles regulated under previous standards» and «2025 for coaches, trailers, and medium lorries»

**Urban buses and trailers.** «the amended Regulation (EU) 2019/1242 mandates that 90% of new city buses must be zero-emission by 2030 and, as of 2035, all new city buses will have to meet the same requirements.» «starting in 2030, CO 2 emissions must be reduced by 10% for new semi-trailers and by 7,5% for new trailers other than semi-trailers.»

**Credits.** «Multi-annual emission credits and debts to balance overachievement of targets in one year with underachievement in another year , accounting for long production cycles.» «Between 2025 and 2029, the super-credits system will be replaced by a benchmark-based crediting system . The benchmark will be set at 2%.»

**Premium.** «Where a manufacturer is found, pursuant to paragraph 2, to have excess CO 2 emissions in a given reporting period from 2025 onwards, the Commission shall impose an excess CO 2 emissions premium, calculated in accordance with the following formula: (excess CO 2 emissions premium) = (excess CO 2 emissions × 4 250 EUR/gCO 2 /tkm).»

**Reporting.** «By 30 September of each year, they shall report those data to the Commission for each new heavy-duty vehicle» «The Commission may impose an administrative fine in each of the following cases: (a) where it finds that the data reported by the manufacturer pursuant to Article 13b of this Regulation deviate from the data resulting from the manufacturer’s records file or the engine type-approval certificate issued within the framework of Regulation (EC) No 595/2009, and the deviation is intentional or due to serious negligence; (b) where the data are not submitted within the deadline referred to in Article 13b(1), second subparagraph, and the delay cannot be duly justified.»

**Scope of the 2019 rules after the revision.** «Regulation (EU) 2019/1242 should be amended in order to cover the same scope as Regulation (EU) 2018/956»

**Vehicles outside the target.** «This paragraph shall not apply to heavy-duty vehicles that are exempted pursuant to Article 6b.»

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «Regulation (EU) 2024/1257 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 24 April 2024 on type-approval of motor vehicles and engines and of systems, components and separate technical units intended for such vehicles, with respect to their emissions and battery durability (Euro 7)», the European Union's Euro 7 vehicle emissions law. Its jurisdictional scope is the whole Union: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» It covers road vehicles and some tyres: «This Regulation applies to motor vehicles of categories M 1 , M 2 , M 3 , N 1 , N 2 and N 3 , as well as trailers of categories O 3 and O 4 as specified in Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2018/858».

What the Regulation says is taken from its own text. What it may mean for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation sets one set of emission and durability rules for new road vehicles, parts and tyres: «This Regulation establishes common technical requirements and administrative provisions for the emission type-approval and market surveillance of motor vehicles, systems, components and separate technical units, with regard to their CO 2 and pollutant emissions, fuel and electric energy consumption and battery durability.» It reaches tyres too: «C 1 , C 2 and C 3 class tyres, as specified in UN Regulation No 117 ( 23 ) , with the exception of ice grip tyres.» It replaces the older emission rules in stages: «Regulation (EC) No 715/2007 is repealed with effect from 1 July 2030. Regulation (EC) No 595/2009 is repealed with effect from 1 July 2031.» «Regulation (EU) 2017/1151 is repealed with effect from 1 July 2030.» «Regulations (EU) No 582/2011 and (EU) 2017/2400, as well as Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/1362 are repealed with effect from 1 July 2031.»

The effective date is set by publication: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .» The record of the Regulation gives the first date of entry into force as «content="2024-05-28"
      datatype="xsd:date"». Application follows later and by vehicle group: «It shall apply from 29 November 2026 for new types of vehicles of categories M 1 and N 1 and components, systems and separate technical units intended for vehicles of categories M 1 or N 1 type-approved under this Regulation and from 29 November 2027 for new vehicles of categories M 1 and N 1 and components, systems and separate technical units for those vehicles.» For categories M 2, M 3, N 2, N 3, O 3 and O 4: «It shall apply from 29 May 2028 for new types of vehicles of categories M 2 , M 3 , N 2 , N 3 , O 3 and O 4 and components, systems and separate technical units intended for vehicles of categories M 2 , M 3 , N 2 , N 3 , O 3 or O 4 type-approved under this Regulation and from 29 May 2029 for new vehicles of categories M 2 , M 3 , N 2 , N 3 , O 3 and O 4 and components, systems and separate technical units for those vehicles.» Tyres follow their own dates: «It shall apply from 1 July 2028 for new types of C 1 class tyres, from 1 April 2030 for new types of C 2 class tyres and from 1 April 2032 for new types of C 3 class tyres.»

*Analytical inference:* a freight business meets this Regulation when it buys, registers, maintains or fits tyres and parts to new vehicles of the listed categories and to trailers. The duties of design and testing sit with manufacturers and public authorities, but the registration dates decide which new vehicles a fleet may put on the road.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: the next date, 29 November 2026, falls inside the next 30 days, but it runs on approval authorities and manufacturers, not on a freight business, and the Regulation states no cost or fee for a vehicle buyer. On the same date a Member State rule starts for parts: «With effect from 29 November 2026, Member States shall prohibit the sale or installation of a system, component or separate technical unit intended to be fitted on a vehicle of category M 1 or N 1 approved under this Regulation, where the system, component or separate technical unit is not type-approved in accordance with this Regulation.» The approval date: «With effect from 29 November 2026, approval authorities shall, in the case of new types of vehicles of category M 1 or N 1 which do not comply with this Regulation, refuse to grant EU emission type-approval or national emission type-approval to such new types of vehicles on grounds relating to CO 2 and pollutant emissions, fuel and electric energy consumption or battery durability.»

- A fleet manager lists every order for a vehicle of category M 1, M 2, M 3, N 1, N 2 or N 3 or a trailer of category O 3 or O 4 that will be registered after 29 November 2027 (categories M 1 and N 1) or after 29 May 2029 (the other categories) and asks the supplier of each, before the order is signed, whether the vehicle type is type-approved under this Regulation.
- A maintenance buyer asks each parts supplier whether replacement pollution control systems and other emission parts for vehicles approved under this Regulation are type-approved, before ordering such parts on or after the dates in Article 11.
- A sustainability analyst asks each vehicle supplier how the vehicle's environmental data, including lifetime values from the on-board monitoring system and the fuel consumption device, will reach the fleet, before the next order for a new vehicle is signed.

The reason for the first step: «With effect from 29 November 2027, national authorities shall, in the case of new vehicles of category M 1 or N 1 which do not comply with this Regulation, consider certificates of conformity to no longer be valid for the purposes of registration and shall prohibit the registration, sale or entry into service of such new vehicles on grounds relating to CO 2 and pollutant emissions, fuel and electric energy consumption or battery durability.» The same rule for categories M 2, M 3, N 2, N 3, O 3 and O 4 starts on 29 May 2029 (Section 8).

*Analytical inference:* the three steps follow from the registration bans and the parts rule quoted in Section 8 and from the user data rule in Section 11. The Regulation names no step for a vehicle buyer; the steps check evidence before a purchase. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a vehicle ordered before these dates but registered after them is caught by the registration ban.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names manufacturers, approval authorities, market surveillance authorities, national authorities, Member States and the Commission. Manufacturers carry the build duty: «Manufacturers shall ensure that the new vehicles that they manufacture, which are sold, registered or enter into service in the Union, are type-approved in accordance with this Regulation.» Approval authorities grant or refuse type-approval, and national authorities decide registration (Section 8). Member States control parts and tyres: «With effect from 29 November 2026, Member States shall prohibit the sale or installation of a system, component or separate technical unit intended to be fitted on a vehicle of category M 1 or N 1 approved under this Regulation, where the system, component or separate technical unit is not type-approved in accordance with this Regulation.» Users appear only as recipients of data: «Environmental data about the vehicle type and the environmental performance of individual vehicles shall be made available to users and, where appropriate, displayed inside the vehicle.» A freight forwarder is not named.

*Analytical inference:* a freight business sits at the end of the chain as buyer, registrant, user and maintainer of vehicles and as a buyer of parts and tyres. The rules that bind it do so through the registration, sale and installation bans on authorities and Member States, not through a duty written for the business. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which party carries the risk, between buyer and supplier, when a vehicle cannot be registered under these rules.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Regulation leaves much to Commission acts and reviews. Acts already due: «By 29 May 2025 the Commission shall adopt for vehicles of categories M 1 and N 1 , as referred to in paragraph 3, point (a), the following implementing acts:» (date passed) and «Where the UN WP.29 has not adopted uniform provisions by 1 July 2026 for C 1 class tyres» (date passed). Due on 29 November 2026: «By 29 November 2026, the Commission shall adopt, for vehicles of categories M 2 , M 3 , N 2 and N 3, as referred to in paragraph 3, points (b) and (c), respectively, and their engines, as well as for trailers of categories O 3 and O 4 , the following implementing acts:».

Items still ahead:
- Tyre abrasion limits: «by 1 July 2027 for C 1 class tyres, by 1 April 2029 for C 2 class tyres and by 1 April 2031 for C 3 class tyres» (delegated acts if the United Nations rules are missing), and the method date «by 1 April 2028 for C 2 class tyres and by 1 April 2030 for C 3 class tyres».
- Reports: «By 31 December 2027, the Commission shall submit to the European Parliament and to the Council a report on battery durability reviewing the state of the art» and «By 31 December 2027, the Commission shall submit to the European Parliament and to the Council a report on brake particle emissions reviewing measuring methods and the state of the art».
- Member States: «By 1 September 2030, Member States shall inform the Commission of the application of this Regulation.»
- Evaluation: «By 1 September 2031, on the basis of the information provided in accordance with paragraph 1, the Commission shall submit to the European Parliament and to the Council an evaluation report on the application of this Regulation».
- Already due: «By 31 December 2025, the Commission shall submit to the European Parliament and to the Council a report assessing the durability performance of heavy-duty vehicles with regard to emissions.» (date passed).

*Analytical inference:* the brake particle report due on 31 December 2027 is the one the text ties to the second-stage brake limits that apply from 1 January 2030, so those limits are not final until that report and the delegated acts are done; the battery durability report concerns the minimum performance requirements for battery durability. The text states what each act or report covers, not its content. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the implementing acts due on 29 May 2025 have been adopted, and which of the later acts exist now.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The first question for a fleet is which date applies to which thing. The Regulation separates a new type of vehicle from a new vehicle. A new type is a design to be approved: «With effect from 29 May 2028, approval authorities shall, in the case of new types of vehicles of category M 2 , M 3 , N 2 or N 3 and new types of trailers of category O 3 or O 4 which do not comply with this Regulation, refuse to grant EU emission type-approval or national emission type-approval to such new types of vehicles and trailers on grounds relating to CO 2 and pollutant emissions, fuel and electric energy consumption or battery durability.» A new vehicle is one to be registered: «With effect from 29 May 2029, national authorities shall, in the case of new vehicles of category M 2 , M 3 , N 2 or N 3 and new trailers of category O 3 or O 4 , which do not comply with this Regulation, consider certificates of conformity to be no longer valid for the purposes of registration and shall prohibit the registration, sale or entry into service of such new vehicles and trailers on grounds relating to CO 2 and pollutant emissions, fuel and electric energy consumption, energy efficiency or battery durability.»

The second question is small-volume makers, who get later dates: «With effect from 1 July 2031, national authorities shall, in the case of new vehicles of category M 2 , M 3 , N 2 or N 3 constructed by small-volume manufacturers, which do not comply with this Regulation, consider certificates of conformity to be no longer valid for the purposes of registration and shall prohibit the registration, sale or entry into service of such new vehicles on grounds relating to CO 2 and pollutant emissions, fuel and electric energy consumption, energy efficiency or battery durability.»

*Analytical inference:* the dates for new types come first and the dates for new vehicles one year later, so a vehicle of an older approved type can still be registered until the new-vehicle date. The category letters are those of Regulation (EU) 2018/858, whose category definitions are not held here. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which category letter applies to each vehicle in the fleet plan, and whether a maker counts as small-volume.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Scope. «This Regulation applies to motor vehicles of categories M 1 , M 2 , M 3 , N 1 , N 2 and N 3 , as well as trailers of categories O 3 and O 4 as specified in Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2018/858».

Build and durability (manufacturers). «Manufacturers shall ensure that the new vehicles that they manufacture, which are sold, registered or enter into service in the Union, are type-approved in accordance with this Regulation.» Durability: «Manufacturers shall ensure that the vehicles that they manufacture, which are sold, registered or enter into service in the Union, comply with the emission limits set out in Annex I when those vehicles are driven under test conditions as set out in Annex III, for the lifetime of the vehicle, as set out in table 1 of Annex IV, and comply with the minimum performance requirements on battery durability as set out in Annex II.» Monitoring equipment: «OBFCM devices to monitor their real-world fuel and electric energy consumption and other relevant parameters, which are needed to determine their real-world fuel and energy efficiency» and «SOH monitors of the traction battery».

Registration bans. «With effect from 29 November 2027, national authorities shall, in the case of new vehicles of category M 1 or N 1 which do not comply with this Regulation, consider certificates of conformity to no longer be valid for the purposes of registration and shall prohibit the registration, sale or entry into service of such new vehicles on grounds relating to CO 2 and pollutant emissions, fuel and electric energy consumption or battery durability.» «With effect from 29 May 2029, national authorities shall, in the case of new vehicles of category M 2 , M 3 , N 2 or N 3 and new trailers of category O 3 or O 4 , which do not comply with this Regulation, consider certificates of conformity to be no longer valid for the purposes of registration and shall prohibit the registration, sale or entry into service of such new vehicles and trailers on grounds relating to CO 2 and pollutant emissions, fuel and electric energy consumption, energy efficiency or battery durability.» For categories M 2 and M 3 there is a step-down: «By way of derogation from paragraph 7 of this Article, until 31 December 2029, national authorities shall allow for vehicles of category M 2 or M 3 , for which there is a 100 % zero-emission target as from the reporting period of the year 2030 in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, the registration, sale or entry into service of new vehicles, which do not comply with this Regulation but have a valid emission type-approval in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 595/2009.»

Parts. «With effect from 29 May 2028, Member States shall prohibit the sale or installation of a system, component or separate technical unit intended to be fitted on a vehicle of category M 2 , M 3 , N 2 or N 3, or on a trailer of category O 3 or O 4 approved under this Regulation, where the system, component or separate technical unit is not type-approved in accordance with this Regulation.» The rule for categories M 1 and N 1 starts on 29 November 2026 (Section 4).

Tyres. «With effect from 1 July 2028, national authorities shall grant component or separate technical unit EU type-approval only in respect of new types of C 1 class tyres which comply with this Regulation. With effect from 1 July 2030, national authorities shall prohibit the placing on the market of C 1 class tyres which do not comply with this Regulation and shall prohibit the registration of new vehicles equipped with C 1 class tyres where those tyres do not comply with this Regulation.» For C 2 and C 3: «With effect from 1 April 2032, national authorities shall prohibit the placing on the market of C 2 class tyres which do not comply with this Regulation and shall prohibit the registration of new vehicles equipped with C 2 class tyres where those tyres do not comply with this Regulation.» and «With effect from 1 April 2034, national authorities shall prohibit the placing on the market of C 3 class tyres which do not comply with this Regulation and shall prohibit the registration of new vehicles equipped with C 3 class tyres where those tyres do not comply with this Regulation.»

Brake particles. The limit steps are set by tables: «Table 7: Euro 7 brake particle emission limits in standard driving cycle applying from 1 January 2030 until 31 December 2034 following the review specifed in Article 18(5), by powertrain technology (vehicles of categories M 3 and N 3 )» and «Table 8: Euro 7 brake particle emission limits in standard driving cycle applying from 1 January 2035 for all powertrain technologies, by vehicle category».

Penalty summary. Article 19 amends Regulation (EU) 2018/858 so that its penalty clause reads: «Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements by economic operators, independent operators, and technical services of this Regulation and shall take all measures necessary to ensure that they are implemented.» «The penalties provided for shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.» No amount of any fine is stated. Listed infringements include «making available on the market vehicles, systems, components or separate technical units subject to approval without such approval, or falsifying documents, certificates of conformity, statutory plates or approval marks with that intention» and «tampering with the vehicle and its systems».

*Analytical inference:* the duties above fall on manufacturers, approval authorities, national authorities and Member States. For a fleet they decide which new vehicles, parts and tyres can be registered, sold or fitted. The text states no price effect, surcharge or pass-through of any compliance cost to a buyer, so how Euro 7 reaches vehicle prices or rates is a gap. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which Member State's penalty rules apply to a business that buys or fits non-approved parts or tyres.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The Regulation sets no registration or report for a freight business. Reporting runs between States, authorities and the Commission: «By 1 September 2030, Member States shall inform the Commission of the application of this Regulation.» The type-approval file is a manufacturer matter: «Procedures for the emission type-approval shall include tests and checks as specified in Annex V as well as all administrative procedures and documentation requirements.» For a buyer the registration step is the national one, and the certificate of conformity decides it: «consider certificates of conformity to no longer be valid for the purposes of registration».

*Analytical inference:* the vehicle registration step is where a fleet meets the Regulation, through the certificate of conformity that the manufacturer supplies. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether national registration practice asks the buyer for any Euro 7 evidence beyond the certificate of conformity.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Regulation builds its system duties into the vehicle and onto manufacturers, and gives users a data right. The user data rule: «Environmental data about the vehicle type and the environmental performance of individual vehicles shall be made available to users and, where appropriate, displayed inside the vehicle. Those data shall cover data from the EVP, the OBM system and the OBFCM device, including lifetime values, and the state of health of the traction battery.» The vehicle must be able to send data off-board: «devices communicating off-board vehicle generated data used for compliance with this Regulation and OBFCM data, including for the purpose of periodic roadworthiness tests in accordance with Directive 2014/45/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 26 ) and technical roadside inspections in accordance with Directive 2014/47/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 27 )».

- A sustainability analyst adds a field to the fleet data sheet for the fuel and energy consumption and battery health values each new vehicle reports, and asks each supplier what format the data comes in, before the first Euro 7 vehicle is accepted.
- A maintenance lead adds to the maintenance job card template, at the next template update, a line that no change is made to the on-board diagnostic, monitoring or fuel consumption systems without a written reason, because tampering with the vehicle and its systems is a listed infringement.

*Analytical inference:* the two steps follow from the user data rule and the penalty list in Section 8. The text states that data must be made available to users but does not state a format, a portal or a charge. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a maintenance provider or the fleet is an independent operator under Regulation (EU) 2018/858, whose definition is not held here.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Several carve-outs and later dates matter for a fleet. Tyres that do not comply may stay on sale for a time: «C 1 class tyres which do not comply with this Regulation may continue to be made available on the market until 30 June 2032.» «C 2 class tyres which do not comply with this Regulation may continue to be made available on the market until 31 March 2034.» «C 3 class tyres which do not comply with this Regulation may continue to be made available on the market until 31 March 2036.» Replacement pollution control systems have an extension route: «Approval authorities may continue to grant extensions to EU emission type-approvals of replacement pollution control systems under the terms which applied at the time of the original emission type approval.» Small-volume makers: «It shall apply from 1 July 2030 for vehicles of categories M 1 and N 1 , constructed by small-volume manufacturers and from 1 July 2031 for vehicles of categories M 2 , M 3 , N 2 and N 3 constructed by small-volume manufacturers.»

*Analytical inference:* the sale-until dates apply to tyres on the market, while the registration bans in the preceding paragraphs apply to new vehicles fitted with non-complying tyres. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether tyres bought before a ban date may still be fitted after it.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2025/40 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 19 December 2024 on packaging and packaging waste, amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and Directive (EU) 2019/904, and repealing Directive 94/62/EC», the European Union's packaging law. Its jurisdictional scope is the whole Union: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» It reaches every kind of packaging: «This Regulation applies to all packaging, regardless of the material used, and to all packaging waste, whether such packaging is used in or such packaging waste originates from industry, other manufacturing, retail or distribution, offices, services or households.»

What the Regulation says is taken from its own text. What it may mean for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation sets one set of rules for packaging across the Union, from design to waste: «This Regulation establishes requirements for the entire life-cycle of packaging as regards environmental sustainability and labelling, to allow its placing on the market.» It enters the transport world in two ways. First, the definition of transport packaging covers the pallets, wraps and boxes that move goods: «‘transport packaging’ means packaging conceived so as to facilitate the handling and transport of one or more sales units or a grouping of sales units, in order to prevent damage to the product from handling and transport, but which excludes road, rail, ship and air containers». Second, the e-commerce part is named: «‘e-commerce packaging’ means transport packaging used to deliver products in the context of sale online or through other means of distance sales to the end user». The Regulation yields to the dangerous goods transport rules: «However, where this Regulation conflicts with Directive 2008/68/EC, Directive 2008/68/EC shall prevail.»

The effective date and the application date are set apart. The Commission's packaging page states: «The Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation 2025/40 (PPWR) entered into force on 11 February 2025 and will generally apply from 12 August 2026». The Regulation itself says: «It shall apply from 12 August 2026.» It also ends the old Directive: «Directive 94/62/EC is repealed with effect from 12 August 2026, with the exception of:»

*Analytical inference:* packaging that a business buys, supplies, fills or handles on a shipment inside the Union is inside the Regulation, and containers themselves are outside the transport packaging definition. The duties fall on the operators the Regulation names (Section 4), not on every party that moves a pallet.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: the Regulation has applied since 12 August 2026, so its first dates are past. No deadline of the Regulation falls on a freight business inside the next 30 days. The nearest dated steps run on public bodies: «By 31 December 2026, the Commission, assisted by the European Chemicals Agency, shall prepare a report on the presence of substances of concern in packaging and packaging components» and «By 12 February 2027, Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements of this Regulation».

- A compliance lead sorts each EU service line (warehousing, packing, dispatch, packaging supply, importing) against the operator roles in Articles 18 to 20 this month and records the answer per service for counsel.
- A warehouse manager lists the storage, handling, packing, addressing and dispatch steps at each EU site that touch packaging, so the list is ready to check against Article 20 at the next site review.
- A procurement lead lists the pallets, crates, boxes, wraps and straps used for EU transport and marks which belong to a re-use system, for the targets that start on 1 January 2030.

The reason for the roles step: «Fulfilment service providers shall ensure that for packaging, whether empty or with a product, that they handle, the conditions during warehousing, handling and packing, addressing or dispatching do not jeopardise the packaging’s compliance with the requirements laid down in or pursuant to Articles 5 to 12.»

*Analytical inference:* the three steps follow from the quoted Article 20 duty and the transport packaging targets in Section 8. They prepare evidence and a list; they do not decide the business's legal role. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given service makes the business a fulfilment service provider, distributor, importer or producer under the Regulation.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation sorts operators into named roles. A producer is a manufacturer, importer or distributor that makes packaging available in set ways: «‘producer’ means any manufacturer, importer or distributor to whom, irrespective of the selling technique used, including by means of distance contracts, one of the following applies:». The wider group is: «‘economic operator’ means the manufacturer, the supplier, the importer, the distributor, the authorised representative, the final distributor and the fulfilment service provider». An importer is defined as «‘importer’ means any natural or legal person established within the Union that places packaging from a third country on the market», and a distributor as «‘distributor’ means any natural or legal person in the supply chain, other than the manufacturer or importer, that makes packaging available on the market».

Each role has a duty. Importers: «Importers shall only place on the market packaging which is in conformity with the requirements laid down in or pursuant to Articles 5 to 12.» Distributors: «Before making packaging available on the market, distributors shall verify that:» the producer is registered, the packaging is labelled and the manufacturer and importer have complied with their documents. Distributors also carry a transport duty: «Distributors shall ensure that, while the packaging, whether empty or with a product, is under their responsibility, the storage or transport conditions do not jeopardise its conformity with the requirements laid down in or pursuant to Articles 5 to 12.» An importer or distributor can become a manufacturer: «Where an importer or a distributor places packaging on the market under its own name or trademark or modifies packaging already placed on the market in a way that could affect compliance with the relevant requirements of this Regulation, that importer or distributor shall be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation». A freight forwarder is not named in the Regulation, and the fulfilment service provider is defined by Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, whose definition is not held here.

*Analytical inference:* a freight business is in the chain only if it takes one of the named roles for a given packaging flow, for example by storing and dispatching packaging for others, by importing packaging or by supplying it under its own name. The same business can hold different roles on different shipments. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which role, if any, the business holds on each flow, and whether the transport duty applies to goods that are only carried.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

The Commission's packaging page points to guidance but the guidance text itself is not held. It lists «Guidelines on the implementation of the Regulation for economic actors and Member States (March 2026)» and «Frequently Asked Questions (March 2026)» as implementation support.

*Analytical inference:* the guidelines and the questions and answers are the Commission's reading of the Regulation and could settle the role questions in Section 4, but no provision of either document is available to quote, so no section-by-section analysis is given. *Legal Confirmation Required:* what the March 2026 guidelines say about fulfilment service providers, distributors and transport packaging.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Regulation leaves many acts to the Commission and the States, with dates. Items already due: «The Commission shall, by 12 February 2026, adopt implementing acts establishing the format for registration in, and reporting to, the register» (a date that has passed), «By 12 July 2025, Member States shall notify the Commission of the names and addresses of the competent authorities» (passed) and «it shall, by 31 December 2025, supply such information to the Commission and the European Chemicals Agency» (passed, a Member State step).

Items still ahead:
- Substances report: «By 31 December 2026, the Commission, assisted by the European Chemicals Agency, shall prepare a report on the presence of substances of concern in packaging and packaging components».
- Recycled content method: «By 31 December 2026, the Commission shall adopt implementing acts establishing the methodology for the calculation and verification of the percentage».
- Guidelines on restricted formats: «By 12 February 2027, the Commission shall publish guidelines, in consultation with Member States and the European Food Safety Authority, which explain Annex V in more detail».
- Re-use method: «By 30 June 2027, the Commission shall adopt implementing acts establishing the methodology for the calculation of the re-use targets set out in Article 29.»
- Recyclability criteria: «By 1 January 2028, the Commission shall, after taking into consideration standards developed by the European standardisation organisations, adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 64».
- Empty space method: «By 12 February 2028, the Commission shall adopt implementing acts to establish the methodology for the calculation of the empty space ratio referred to in paragraph 1.»
- Public procurement: «by 12 February 2030, adopt implementing acts specifying minimum mandatory requirements for public contracts».
- PFAS review: «By 12 August 2030, the Commission shall carry out an evaluation to assess the need to amend or repeal this paragraph».
- Re-use jobs data: «By December 2032, Member States shall provide data to the Commission on the employment impact assessment related to the implementation of the re-use targets in their national territories.»
- Biobased plastic review: «By 12 February 2028, the Commission shall review the state of technological development and environmental performance of biobased plastic packaging, taking into consideration the sustainability criteria laid down in Article 29 of Directive (EU) 2018/2001 of the European Parliament and of the Council».
- Reviews: «By 12 February 2032, the Commission shall review the empty space ratio referred to in paragraph 1», «By 12 August 2033, the Commission shall carry out an evaluation to assess whether this Article and the design for recycling criteria», «By 1 January 2034, taking into account the evolution of the state of the art of technology and the practical experience gained by economic operators and Member States, the Commission shall present a report reviewing the implementation of the 2030 targets set out in this Article» and «By 12 August 2034, the Commission shall carry out an evaluation of this Regulation».

The text states what each act is to cover, not its content. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any of these acts has been adopted since the Regulation was published.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The first question is who the Regulation treats as the producer, because registration follows from it (Section 10). The definition has five limbs, the first two for a business established in a Member State that makes packaging available for the first time from there, the next two for a business that sells directly to end users in another Member State, and the last for a business that unpacks packaged products without being an end user: «(e) the manufacturer, importer or distributor is established in a Member State and unpacks packaged products without being an end user, unless another person is the producer as defined in point (a), (b), (c) or (d);».

The second question is what counts as making packaging available: «‘making available on the market’ means any supply of packaging, whether empty or with a product, for distribution, consumption or use on the Union market in the course of a commercial activity, whether in return for payment or free of charge».

The third question is whether a good is excluded as an end user: «‘end user’ means any natural or legal person that resides or is established in the Union to whom a product has been made available either as a consumer or as a professional end user in the course of its industrial or professional activities, and that does not make that product further available on the market in the form supplied to it».

*Analytical inference:* a business that only carries sealed packaged goods for another party does not obviously supply or unpack them, and the definitions do not mention carriage. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether carriage, storage or unpacking on a client's behalf is making available or unpacking within these definitions.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Hazardous substances. Heavy metals are capped: «the sum of the concentrations of lead, cadmium, mercury and hexavalent chromium resulting from substances present in packaging or packaging components shall not exceed 100 mg/kg». PFAS in food-contact packaging are limited from the application date: «From 12 August 2026, food-contact packaging shall not be placed on the market if it contains per- and polyfluorinated alkyl substances (PFAS) in a concentration equal to or above the following limit values».

Recyclability. «All packaging placed on the market shall be recyclable.» The grades apply in steps: «from 1 January 2030 or 24 months from the entry into force of the delegated acts adopted pursuant to paragraph 4 of this Article, whichever is the latest, packaging shall not be placed on the market unless it is recyclable within grades A, B or C as described in Table 3 of Annex II» and «from 1 January 2038 packaging shall not be placed on the market unless it is recyclable within grades A or B as described in Table 3 of Annex II». The recycled-at-scale test follows: «Point (b) of the first subparagraph of this paragraph shall apply from 1 January 2035».

Recycled content in plastic. «By 1 January 2030 or 3 years from the date of entry into force of the implementing act referred to in paragraph 8 of this Article, whichever is the latest, any plastic part of packaging placed on the market shall contain the following minimum percentage of recycled content recovered from post-consumer plastic waste», with «(d) 35 % for plastic packaging other than those referred to in points (a), (b) and (c) of this paragraph» from the 2030 step and «(d) 65 % for plastic packaging other than those referred to in points (a), (b) and (c) of this paragraph» by «By 1 January 2040».

Packaging size and empty space. «By 1 January 2030, the manufacturer or importer shall ensure that the packaging placed on the market is designed so that its weight and volume is reduced to the minimum necessary to ensure its functionality». For transport use: «By 1 January 2030 or 3 years from the entry into force of the implementing acts adopted pursuant to paragraph 2, whichever is the latest, economic operators who fill grouped packaging, transport packaging or e-commerce packaging shall ensure that the maximum empty space ratio, expressed as a percentage, is 50 %». Space filled by cushioning counts as empty: «Space filled by filling materials, such as paper cuttings, air cushions, bubble wraps, sponge fillers, foam fillers, wood wool, polystyrene or Styrofoam chips, shall be considered as empty space.» Sales packaging has an earlier date: «By 12 February 2028, the economic operators who fill sales packaging shall ensure that empty space is reduced to the minimum necessary for ensuring the packaging functionality, including product protection.»

Labelling. «packaging placed on the market shall be marked with a harmonised label containing information on its material composition in order to facilitate consumer sorting», and «With the exception of e-commerce packaging, this obligation does not apply to transport packaging or to packaging that is subject to a deposit and return system.» Reusable packaging: «Reusable packaging placed on the market from 12 February 2029 or 30 months from the date of entry into force of the implementing act adopted pursuant to paragraph 6, whichever is the latest, shall bear a label informing users that the packaging is reusable.»

Restricted formats. «From 1 January 2030, economic operators shall not place on the market packaging in the formats and for the uses listed in Annex V.»

Re-use of transport packaging. «From 1 January 2030, economic operators that use transport packaging, or sales packaging used for transporting products, including for products distributed via e-commerce, within the territory of the Union, in the form of pallets, foldable-plastic boxes, boxes, trays, plastic crates, intermediate bulk containers, pails, drums and canisters of any size or material, including flexible formats or pallet wrappings or straps for stabilisation and protection of products put on pallets during transport, shall ensure that at least 40 % of such packaging in total is reusable packaging within a re-use system.» Two cases rise to full re-use: «economic operators that use transport packaging or sales packaging used for transporting products, in the forms as listed in paragraph 1 of this Article, within the territory of the Union, between different sites on which the operator performs its activity» and, for deliveries within one Member State, «to deliver products to another economic operator within the same Member State shall ensure that such packaging is reusable within a re-use system». The 2040 step is softer: «From 1 January 2040, those economic operators shall endeavour to use at least 70 % of the packaging referred to in the first subparagraph in a reusable format within a re-use system.»

Re-use reporting. «Economic operators as referred to in Article 29(1) to (8) shall submit a report containing data concerning the achievement of the re-use targets set out in Article 29 for each calendar year to the competent authority referred to in Article 40.» «The report referred to in paragraph 1 shall be submitted within 6 months from the end of the reporting year for which the data are collected.» «The first reporting year shall concern the calendar year 2030.» The text gives no calendar date for the first report; six months after the end of 2030 is derived from these sentences.

Member State targets. «by 31 December 2025, a minimum of 65 % by weight of all packaging waste generated» and «by 31 December 2030, a minimum of 70 % by weight of all packaging waste generated». Deposit systems: «If the 90 % target is not achieved by 1 January 2029, existing single-use deposit and return systems shall comply with the minimum requirements in Annex X at the latest by 1 January 2035.» The 90 % target: «By 1 January 2029, Member States shall take the necessary measures to ensure the separate collection of at least 90 % per year by weight of the following packaging formats».

Waste prevention. «Each Member State shall reduce the packaging waste generated per capita, as compared to the packaging waste generated per capita in 2018 as reported to the Commission in accordance with Decision 2005/270/EC, by at least: (a) 5 % by 2030; (b) 10 % by 2035; (c) 15 % by 2040.» Old rules end in stages: «Decision 97/129/EC is repealed with effect from 12 August 2028.»

Penalty summary. «By 12 February 2027, Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements of this Regulation and shall take all measures necessary to ensure that they are implemented.» «The penalties provided for shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.» «The penalties for failure to comply with Articles 24 to 29 shall include administrative fines.» No amount of any fine is stated. Where non-compliance persists the Member State acts: «Where the non-compliance referred to in paragraph 1, points (a) to (f), persists, the Member State concerned shall take all appropriate measures to prohibit the packaging from being made available on the market or to ensure that the packaging is recalled or withdrawn from the market.»

*Analytical inference:* the duties above fall on the named operators and on Member States. For a freight business the closest are the transport packaging targets (pallets, crates, wraps, straps) and the empty space ratio, which apply to economic operators that use or fill such packaging. The Regulation states no price effect, surcharge or pass-through of any of these costs to a client, so how they reach a quote is a gap. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is an economic operator for each duty, and which Member State's fining rules apply.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Producers must be on a national register: «Producers shall be obliged to register in the register referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article in each Member State where they make packaging or packaged products available on the territory of the Member State for the first time or where they unpack packaged products without being end users». The consequence of not registering: «Producers shall not make available packaging or packaged products on the territory of a Member State for the first time, or unpack packaged products without being end users, if they or, where applicable, in accordance with Article 45, their authorised representatives for the extended producer responsibility are not registered in that Member State.» The registers themselves are due in steps: «Each Member State shall, within 18 months of the date of entry into force of first implementing act adopted pursuant to paragraph 14, establish a national register». A producer from another State or a third country that sells to end users must appoint a representative: «A producer referred to in Article 3(1), point (15)(c) and (d), shall appoint, by written mandate, an authorised representative for the extended producer responsibility in each Member State where the producer makes packaging or packaged products available for the first time, other than the Member State where the producer is established.» Producers carry extended producer responsibility: «Producers shall have extended producer responsibility under the schemes established in accordance with Articles 8 and 8a of Directive 2008/98/EC and with this Section for the packaging, including packaging of packaged products, that they make available for the first time on the territory of a Member State or that they unpack without being end users.» Member States also report: «Member States shall, by 12 February 2027, notify the Commission of the rules and measures referred to in paragraph 1 and 2».

*Analytical inference:* registration and extended producer responsibility attach to the producer role, not to carriage as such. A business that is a producer in a Member State registers there before it first makes packaging available. The text states no registration fee or amount. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is a producer in any Member State and whether it needs an authorised representative.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Regulation applies now, and most system work falls on manufacturers and importers, but three records matter to a business that buys, supplies or handles packaging.

- A packaging buyer asks each packaging supplier for the EU declaration of conformity and the technical documentation reference for each packaging type before the next purchase order, because an importer or manufacturer without them is non-compliant.
- A quality lead adds a check at goods-in and dispatch that the label and any QR code or data carrier on packaging is readable, because a data carrier that gives no access to the required information is a listed non-compliance.
- A fleet and warehouse planner records, per pallet, crate and wrap type, who owns it and which re-use system it belongs to, ready for the 1 January 2030 targets.

The text behind the first two steps: «Importers shall indicate on the packaging their name and their registered trade name or registered trademark as well as the postal address at which and, where available, the electronic means of communication by which they can be contacted.» and «the QR code or data carrier referred to in Article 12 do not provide access to the information required in accordance with that Article». Compliance is shown in a file: «Compliance with the requirements set out in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article shall be demonstrated in the technical documentation referred to in Annex VII».

*Analytical inference:* the three steps are record-keeping that supports the roles in Section 4. The Regulation requires nothing of a carrier for these records. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business must hold or check the conformity documents for packaging it only handles.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Several carve-outs matter for transport. Re-use targets for transport packaging do not apply to: «The obligations set out in paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 do not apply to transport packaging or sales packaging:» «(a) used for the transportation of dangerous goods in accordance with Directive 2008/68/EC;» «(b) used for the transportation of large-scale machinery, equipment and commodities for which packaging is custom-designed to fit the individual requirements of the economic operator that made the order;» and «(d) in the form of cardboard boxes.» The empty space duty has its own exemption: «Economic operators using sales packaging as e-commerce packaging or using reusable packaging within a system of re-use shall be exempt from the obligation laid down in paragraph 1 of this Article.» Small firms get a limited derogation: «Member States may allow micro-enterprises as defined in Recommendation 2003/361/EC as applicable on 11 February 2025 to place on the market packaging in the formats and for the uses listed in point 3 of Annex V».

*Analytical inference:* the dangerous goods and custom-designed packaging exclusions would remove those packaging flows from the 1 January 2030 re-use targets, but only where the wording is met. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular consignment meets the dangerous goods or custom-designed wording.
